name: Transcript access by pages and by streamed MessagePort for long conversations
what: The UI can read a conversation's transcript in pages, from the tail, or as a stream over a port, which keeps long sessions responsive.
how: LocalSessions exposes getTranscript, getTranscriptTail, getTranscriptPage, readTranscript and requestTranscriptPort; the preload relays the "transcript:port" message with transferred ports to the page; the main side forks a transcript worker per request and raises TRANSCRIPT_PORT_MISSING if a port is not supplied; thinking-summary wanted flags and side-chat/btw child sessions run alongside.

verevonRelevance: Model Plane should offer windowed transcript reads plus a streaming channel so the web UI can virtualise long chats.

name: Dictation through a short-lived streaming credential and a dedicated CSP
what: Voice input streams audio to a speech service using a credential the host obtains on demand, with the page's CSP allowing only the configured endpoint.
how: Dictation.getStreamCredential returns the credential; in third-party mode the dictation endpoint is added to the per-response CSP (dictationCsp); flags quickEntryDictation and customQuickEntryDictationShortcut control the shortcut; microphone permission and admin restriction messages are localised.

name: Web search/fetch gating by org flags, per-surface settings and domain preflight
what: Web tools can be switched off per surface, are subject to org policy, and WebFetch does a domain preflight that admins can skip.
how: Preference coworkWebSearchEnabled (default true), registry key skipWebFetchPreflight, organisation flags such as web_search_mcp_isolation in the org flag list, and egress allow-lists for sandboxed processes combine; web_search and WebFetch are part of the default Cowork tool list.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane should treat web tools as policy-controlled capabilities with an explicit preflight step and sandbox egress rules.
notes: This desktop host does not implement search itself; it relies on the engine and server tools.

name: Claude Code CLI as the agent engine, driven through the Agent SDK over stdio
what: Code and Cowork sessions are not implemented in the desktop app: the app launches the Claude Code engine (the same engine as the terminal CLI) as a child process and drives it with the Agent SDK, which streams messages and tool-permission requests back.
how: The lazy-loaded SDK chunk (claude-agent-sdk 0.3.295) builds the CLI environment (CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT defaults sdk-ts, CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION, CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING, CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_READS_SESSION_STATE, CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_HAS_OAUTH_REFRESH / HAS_HOST_AUTH_REFRESH, trace context propagation) and spawns the native binary named by pathToClaudeCodeExecutable. The desktop passes its own executable path, an empty executableArgs list, model, effort, maxTurns, cwd, hooks and tool lists. Entry point values recognised for session classification include sdk-cli, sdk-ts, sdk-py, local-agent, claude-desktop, remote_cowork.
verevonRelevance: Verevon can reuse the same split for its coding agent: keep the loop in a separately versioned engine process and implement host concerns (permissions, mounts, credentials, UI) as SDK callbacks.
notes: DOC: code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop confirms the Code tab runs its own app-managed copy of Claude Code. The CLI binary itself is Bun-compiled (error classifiers match "Bun has crashed").

name: Host integration seam: a custom spawn function lets the same engine run locally, in a VM or over SSH
what: Where the engine process actually runs (this PC, the Cowork VM, a remote SSH host) is decided by a pluggable spawn function; the SDK and UI code stay identical.
how: The SDK option spawnClaudeCodeProcess is set per session: for VM sessions createVMSpawnFunction returns an EventEmitter-like process whose stdin is forwarded and whose stdout/stderr/exit come from the VM client's event stream (the OAuth token is stripped from env and passed as a separate spawn argument); for SSH sessions backend.createSpawnFunction(stderr, onProcessLoss, onReattachGap, ...) tunnels to the remote helper and supports reattach. Process handles expose confirmSpawn, setError, setExited and failedMounts.
verevonRelevance: This is the key abstraction for Verevon's Model Plane sandboxes: one agent-process interface with local/VM/remote backends so run semantics never depend on where the process lives.

name: Session options builder: tool allow-lists, effort clamping and host-delivered OAuth
what: Each Cowork/Code session is configured centrally: which built-in tools exist and are pre-allowed, how long it may run, which model and effort it uses, and how the engine refreshes its token without the token being in the environment.
how: The builder returns {cwd:"/sessions/<id>" (VM), model, effort (clamped through clampSessionEffort for the surface), maxTurns by session type, pathToClaudeCodeExecutable, getOAuthToken (a refresh callback), tools:[Task,Bash,Glob,Grep,Read,Edit,Write,NotebookEdit,WebFetch,WebSearch,Skill,REPL,JavaScript,AskUserQuestion,Artifact?,ToolSearch,SendUserMessage? ...], allowedTools,...}; VM egress domains are resolved per spawn (resolveVmAllowedDomains) and an OTLP config is generated per spawn for the VM target; agent sessions default allowedTools to include ToolSearch and mcp__computer-use.
verevonRelevance: Centralise per-surface tool sets and effort clamps in one Model Plane "run profile" builder rather than scattering them across UI handlers.

name: Permission callback with forged-card defence, escalation and unattended denial messages
what: Tool permission decisions are made in the host. A tool call whose name imitates an internal approval card is rejected, risky asks can be escalated to a person, and unattended runs get a clear refusal that tells the model what it can still do.
how: canUseTool first denies names that match card-style ask names ("Denying forged card-named ask", "No such tool."), then applies surface gates (HIPAA, onboarding picker), then escalation logic (escalatedForPerson, kill switch flag, ownTurnUnattended, isDispatchChild, parentTurnUnattended). For computer-use tools it returns allow/updatedInput, an approval card, or deny with instructive messages (unattended_no_approver, feature_disabled, "steer to request_access"). Outcomes are logged as lam_escalated_tool_ask with card or unattended_deny.
verevonRelevance: Verevon approval flows should (1) never trust model-supplied tool names that collide with UI card names, (2) distinguish attended from unattended runs, and (3) return denial text that redirects the model, which reduces retry loops.
notes: Instructive denial text is part of the defence: it steers the model to alternatives instead of failing silently.

name: In-process SDK MCP servers expose host tools to the engine without separate processes
what: Built-in capabilities (computer use, memory, spaces inventory, plugin search, file upload, browser tools, etc.) are MCP servers created inside the desktop process and passed to the engine as type "sdk" servers.
how: createSdkMcpServer yields {type:"sdk",name,instance}; Query.captureSdkMcpServerManifests performs an initialize and tools/list against each SDK server to cache manifests; names such as computer-use, computer, browser_batch, cowork, spaces-inventory, memory, design, skills, git, file-index appear in the host. An allowlist/denylist pair (tools, allowedTools, disallowedTools) plus the mcp__<server>__<tool> naming convention govern exposure.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane should offer in-process tool servers for latency-sensitive built-ins and keep the MCP naming scheme so the same policy engine governs built-in and third-party tools.

name: Session record model and origin kinds across chat, Cowork, Code and CLI
what: All kinds of conversations share one local session table with typed origins, so Cowork, Code, chat and imported terminal sessions can be listed, searched, archived and resumed together.
how: Session ids use a local_ prefix; storage lives in claude-code-sessions (Code) and local-agent-mode-sessions (Cowork) with an archived-sessions.idx and an imported-staging area; origin kinds are claude-ai-chat, local-1p-cowork, local-1p-chat, local-1p-code and terminal-cli, with prefixes like previous-profile- and sibling-1p- for carried-over data; session types include agent, dispatch_child, scheduled and chat. Imported sessions are blocked until the user chooses "trust and resume".
verevonRelevance: Verevon's session model should record an origin kind and a trust state for imported/carried-over histories so resume cannot silently replay untrusted tool calls.

name: Message delivery state machine: uuid echo, held steers, deferred sends, replay after loss
what: Messages typed while the agent is busy are queued, steered into the running turn, or held across a lost connection, and every one has a stable uuid so it is neither lost nor sent twice.
how: Session state keeps pendingCycle (userMessageUuid, ownPromptDequeued, hadFirstResponse, promptLifecycle), deferredSends, heldSteers, heldAcrossLoss, coalescedDrain, pendingEchoUuids and writtenUnackedUuids; after a reattach gap the host rebuilds the message buffer from the uuid sets, re-seeds the transcript from the remote file and emits a local_command_output notice if the gap cannot be filled. Public IPC verbs: sendMessage, sendSteeredNow, promoteQueuedMessage, reorderQueuedMessage, cancelQueuedMessage.
evidence: claude:tmp/claude-audit/eipc_services_v3.txt (scout parser output of the 89 eipc service definitions; cross-checked against ao() calls in index.chunk-EzXl5k4A.js~L45753-L45876)
verevonRelevance: Verevon's run/session service should give every user and tool message a uuid, track echo/ack state and make steer/queue semantics explicit; this is hard to retrofit.
notes: State field semantics were inferred from names and surrounding code.

name: SSH sessions survive disconnects: remote helper daemon, sequence replay and orphan reaping
what: If the SSH link drops mid-turn the remote engine process keeps running; on reconnect the desktop reattaches, replays missed frames from a sequence number and either resumes the turn or explains what was lost.
how: Per-session fields (sshRemoteProcessId, sshReattach {processId,hostKey,inputPending,midTurn}, sshOrphanProcesses with eviction cap, sshLoss, sshRecoverAfterProcessLoss) drive a loss handler that classifies kinds (abandoned, killed_attached, foreign_daemon) and causes, applies a process-loss brake (rule, losses this round, rounds per hour) and limiter before auto-restarting, and reaps orphans with kill escalation (confirmed, waited-survivor). Telemetry events record reattach_ms, detached_ms, replayed_frames, replayed_bytes, from_seq/first_seq gaps. The bridge-session record carries lastSequenceNum.
verevonRelevance: For long-running Verevon agents on remote runners, copy the model: durable remote process identity, sequence-numbered event log with replay, explicit orphan reaping and a restart brake to avoid kill loops.
notes: DOC: SSH sessions run on a remote Linux or macOS machine and the app installs Claude Code there on first connect (code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop).

name: Remote helper controller with deferred upgrade and org-required launcher
what: The helper installed on a remote host is versioned and upgraded by the desktop, but replacement waits until running sessions there are quiet, and an organisation can require that Claude Code is started through a specific launcher.
how: RemoteServerController tracks helperReplaceable, ourHelperVersionAtConnect, forceDaemonReplace, helperUpdateRefusedSinceConnect and managedLauncherApplied; messages explain that an older helper is replaced at a later launch once sessions go quiet, and refusal when "No launcher is named in Claude Code's managed settings". A restartHelperNow path exists for users. Host power state (sleep) is consulted so connects can be judged sleep-interrupted.
verevonRelevance: Same versioned-daemon pattern applies to any Verevon runner agent installed on customer hosts: upgrade only at quiescence and expose the managed-launcher hook.

name: SSH transport duality: pure-JS ssh2 or the system OpenSSH, plus askpass broker and verified host keys
what: SSH environments can connect either with a bundled ssh2 client or by shelling out to the system OpenSSH (Microsoft OpenSSH 9.4+ on Windows), with a password helper that verifies the prompt really comes from the host-key-verified ssh process.
how: sshTransport is "openssh" or ssh2; usesOpenSshEngine is true for openssh; admin settings can force the client; claude-ssh-askpass.exe and claude-ssh-broker.exe (Go, named pipe with a security descriptor) mediate passphrase/password prompts back to the UI, and remembered answers are replayed only if askerVerified and verifiedHostKey match and policy does not disable saved passwords; claude-ssh-proxy.exe provides a ProxyCommand-style relay.
evidence: claude:install resources claude-ssh-askpass.exe / claude-ssh-broker.exe / claude-ssh-proxy.exe (Go, module anthropics/ssh-askpass)
verevonRelevance: Verevon's remote runner onboarding can learn from the askpass-broker design (never type secrets into a terminal the agent can read).

name: Error taxonomy for engine failures with targeted recovery messages
what: Failures of the engine process, the stream or the network are classified into specific categories so the UI shows an actionable message and the host chooses retry, resume or give up.
how: Classifiers match process exit codes (Windows 0xC0000409 fastfail, DLL-not-found, interrupted codes), Bun crash/stack-overflow output, exec-format errors, stdin-write-after-exit errors, query-closed errors and SDK errorClass values (process_exited_nonzero, process_killed_by_signal, spawn_failed, executable_not_found, aborted, control_request_failed); stream stall regexes ("response stopped arriving", idle timeout), API 400 variants (strict sandbox, auto mode), gateway sign-in errors (gateway_signin_required, gateway_access_denied) and unreachable API messages.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's run engine should keep a closed error-category enum with user-facing copy per category; the Windows fastfail/DLL mapping is a practical detail often missed.

name: Sleep-aware stall handling and wake accounting
what: If the laptop sleeps mid-response the app recognises that and does not report a model failure; remote-reachability features re-check after resume.
how: Message classifiers detect "went to sleep mid-response" and "while your computer was asleep" and treat them as recoverable; the remote-control module listens to powerMonitor suspend/resume, runs a 30-second "still awake" check and reconciles state; reconnect decisions use a host power ledger.
verevonRelevance: Local-device runs in Verevon must tolerate suspend/resume without marking runs failed.

name: Keep-awake claims and a Stay-reachable mode with an OS wake helper
what: The machine is kept awake while work is running, and an optional mode keeps it reachable for remote requests by scheduling wake-ups, backing off on battery.
how: A powerSaveBlocker("prevent-app-suspension") is acquired by named claims; the remote-serving controller has modes wake_helper, keep_awake_fallback and off, uses different wake intervals on AC and battery, holds a session sleep assertion while a wake is serving, and releases when on battery; preferences ccKeepAwakeWhileWorking and ccKeepAwakeOnBattery gate it.
verevonRelevance: Desktop Verevon agents that continue work while the lid is closed need the same claims model plus battery-aware limits.

name: Scheduled tasks stored as local files with host runs, approvals and watcher history
what: Recurring or one-off tasks are saved on the machine, run in sessions of type "scheduled", and ask for tool approvals with a configurable lifetime.
how: scheduled-tasks.json lives under userData (and per account/session roots); CCDScheduledTasks (12 methods) and CoworkScheduledTasks (16 methods) manage create/update/status/file content, removeApprovedPermission, getWatcherHistory, ack/dispatch-claim methods; a ScheduledTasksManager stamps remote migration links; mcpScheduledTaskApprovalLifetimeDays controls how long approvals last; cronstrue renders cron text; the engine's own cron can be disabled (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON) for sessions that must not self-schedule.
evidence: claude:tmp/claude-audit/eipc_services_v3.txt (scout parser output of the 89 eipc service definitions; cross-checked against ao() calls in index.chunk-EzXl5k4A.js~L45753-L45876)
verevonRelevance: Model Plane schedules should keep per-task approval lifetimes and a dispatch-claim/ack protocol so two devices never run the same task.
notes: The scheduler's trigger loop was not located; it may live in the engine or a chunk without an obvious name.

name: Dispatch: phone-started sessions with unattended-turn policy and short-lived computer-use grants
what: A paired phone or claude.ai can start sessions on the computer; those sessions run unattended and get stricter, time-limited computer-use approvals.
how: GrandPrix (pair/disconnect/request/verification codes) and the RemoteControlServing service bind devices; session types include dispatch_child; permission logic treats a dispatch child as unattended when its parent turn is unattended; computer-use grants for dispatch sessions have a TTL (getChicagoDispatchCuGrantTtlMs, default 30 minutes per DOC) and expired grants are pruned at turn start.
evidence: claude:tmp/claude-audit/eipc_services_v3.txt (scout parser output of the 89 eipc service definitions; cross-checked against ao() calls in index.chunk-EzXl5k4A.js~L45753-L45876)
DOC code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop (computer use: approvals last 30 minutes for Dispatch-spawned sessions)
verevonRelevance: For Verevon mobile-to-desktop dispatch, time-boxed grants plus an explicit unattended flag are a good default.

name: File-state checkpoints and rewind via SDK checkpointing and a shadow git repository
what: Users can rewind a conversation and the files to an earlier point, undo the rewind, and fork a session; file states are captured without touching the user's own git history.
how: The SDK is started with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING; the host exposes rewind, rewindV2, rewindFiles, undoRewind, switchRewindMark, rewindToRefusedPrompt, forkSession; a git-shadow root under userData holds shadow git directories that share objects with the real repo (GIT_COMMON_DIR/GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY) but use a private index and refs, with posture-specific command policies and self-checks.
evidence: claude:tmp/claude-audit/eipc_services_v3.txt (scout parser output of the 89 eipc service definitions; cross-checked against ao() calls in index.chunk-EzXl5k4A.js~L45753-L45876)
verevonRelevance: A shadow-repo approach gives Verevon cheap, git-compatible checkpoints for agent file edits without polluting the user's branches.
notes: Exact checkpoint creation points were not traced.

name: Warm VM between turns with an idle grace period
what: The sandbox VM stays alive for a short idle window after a turn so follow-up messages start fast, then is released.
how: Session spawn passes keptWarmBetweenTurns = !oneShot && idleGraceMs() > 0 to the OTLP/env builder; one-shot VM processes exist for tools; a VM restart path is triggered by user request or heartbeat failure and joins an in-flight restart instead of starting a second one.
verevonRelevance: Sandbox pooling with an idle grace period is the obvious latency optimisation for Verevon runners.

name: Transcript search and inference-log extraction in a dedicated worker
what: Searching past conversations scans local transcript files off the main thread and can extract server inference-log ids for support.
how: transcript-search-worker handles search (returns sessionId, snippet, lastActivityAt), readTranscript and extractInferenceLogIds using node:readline over line-delimited records and a parentPort protocol with request ids.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane transcripts should record inference/request ids so a support bundle can correlate a run with provider logs.

name: Remote Control serving: local folders registered as remote environments with polling and registration states
what: Folders on the computer can be "served" to other devices as environments; the desktop registers them, keeps them in sync, queues deletions and re-registers when the tool-host advertisement changes.
how: A serving controller tracks per-folder records (path, environmentId, registration unregistered|registered|failed, toolHostAdvertised, toolHostBlocker such as git_unknown or gate_off, keys), a no-folder "machine" record for starts without a folder, persisted state with pendingDelete queues, announce baselines for folders auto-added, polling timers and registration retry; it integrates with the wake helper so the machine stays reachable.
evidence: claude:tmp/claude-audit/eipc_services_v3.txt (scout parser output of the 89 eipc service definitions; cross-checked against ao() calls in index.chunk-EzXl5k4A.js~L45753-L45876)
verevonRelevance: For Verevon Spaces on desktop, registering local folders as named environments (with ids and advertised capabilities) is a workable way to let web/mobile sessions target them.
notes: The remote API contract for registration was not inspected.

name: Two execution modes: host-native loop (default) versus full-VM agent loop
what: By default the agent loop and file tools run on the user's computer with path-based access control while shell commands run inside the VM; admins can require the entire loop to run in the VM.
how: The registry key requireCoworkFullVmSandbox (fail-closed true, warn text explains the trade-off: host-native "starts faster and works behind restricted networks") selects full-VM mode; at runtime isHostLoopModeEnabled, isHostLoopDevOverrideActive and setForceDisableHostLoop (preference forceDisableHostLoop) switch modes, session state carries hostLoopMode and hostLoopRequired flags, plugin roots are staged for host-loop hooks (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} symlink staging), and managed MDM changes are logged as desktop_enterprise_host_mode_changed.
evidence: DOC code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop (requireCoworkFullVmSandbox controls the full VM sandbox for Cowork)
verevonRelevance: A two-tier sandbox policy (fast host-native default, stricter full-VM option for regulated tenants) is a design Verevon can offer per tenant: same agent API, different placement of the loop and file tools.
notes: Which tools run on the host in host-native mode beyond file tools was not enumerated.

name: MCP configuration file with per-server fault isolation and visible skip reporting
what: MCP servers are defined in claude_desktop_config.json; one broken entry does not stop the others, and the user is told which entries were skipped.
how: The config lives in userData (candidate roots include Roaming and Local data of both Claude and Claude Nest); loading validates each server entry against its schema individually (Dut filters invalid servers into invalidServers), shows a dialog listing skipped names (truncated to 10, 40 chars each) and logs a desktop_config_load outcome event; malformed JSON shows "Couldn't load app settings"; the Code tab merges these servers with ~/.claude.json and .mcp.json (config-file definition wins for duplicate names per DOC) and settings gate user-added servers (isLocalDevMcpEnabled), tool-call timeout (mcpToolTimeoutSec) and tool search (toolSearchEnabled).
evidence: DOC code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop (MCP servers from the Claude Desktop chat app, fetched 2026-10-13)
verevonRelevance: Adopt per-entry validation with a skip report for Verevon connector/MCP config; partial availability beats a hard failure at startup.

name: Direct MCP host: a utility process that proxies a remote MCP server over a MessagePort and handles OAuth refresh and elicitation
what: Remote (HTTP/SSE) MCP servers are reached through a dedicated process that re-exports them locally, so the engine only sees a simple local server while the desktop owns authentication, retries and network settings.
how: The main process sends {type:"addServer", config} plus a port to directMcpHost.js; it connects an MCP client (streamable HTTP or SSE, Electron net.fetch so system proxy and certificates apply, connect and tools-discovery timeouts, optional versionNegotiation probe that falls back if a middlebox defeats it), lists tools, posts {type:"ready",tools} and then runs an MCP Server over the port transport exposing tools/list, tools/call (with per-server toolCallTimeoutMs; errors returned as isError text), resources/list and resources/read; 401s are routed back to main as authRejected with sequence numbers so credentials can be refreshed; elicitation/create and elicitation-complete are forwarded to the UI; a 404 on the Mcp-Session-Id closes the port so it re-parks; three consecutive terminal errors close the connection.
evidence: claude:index.chunk-EzXl5k4A.js eipc MCP/Extensions services (authorizeDirectMcpServer, directMcpCallTool: scout inventory section 3 category 5)
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Model Plane should proxy third-party MCP servers through a local supervised process too, so OAuth, proxies, retries and elicitation live in one place and the agent sees stable tools.
notes: The re-export hides the remote server's identity from the engine; per-tool policy (managed ask lists) is applied in the host (INF from getManagedAskToolNames).

name: Node-based extensions run inside the app's own Node (utility process) with stdin/stdout virtualised and self-exec blocked
what: Desktop extensions written for Node run without the user installing Node: the app starts them inside an Electron utility process, wires their stdio to a MessagePort and blocks them from re-launching the app binary.
how: mcp-runtime/nodeHost.js receives an init message with a port, replaces process.stdout/stderr.write with posts to the port, makes process.stdin a Readable fed by "stdin" messages, then dynamic-imports the extension entry point with a faked argv ("node", entry, ...). A guard patches child_process.spawn/spawnSync/execFileSync/execSync/execFile: any attempt to run the Electron executable (or app helper binaries) as Node is redirected to a non-existent ".built-in-node-refused" file and surfaces ERR_MCP_NODE_HOST_NOT_NODE with advice to install Node and disable "Use built-in Node.js for MCP"; repeated refusals throw; fatal errors are posted to the parent. Settings: setIsUsingBuiltInNodeForMcp. The fork injects NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1 and per-target proxy env.
verevonRelevance: A Rust host cannot embed Node, but the pattern generalises: run extension servers in a supervised runtime with a recursion guard so a tool cannot launch another copy of the host.

name: MCPB/DXT extension manifest schema (v0.1 to v0.4) and install pipeline
what: Extensions are zip bundles with a manifest declaring server type, launch command, user configuration, tools/prompts and compatibility; the app installs them from a file, a folder, an unpacked directory, a directory listing or a preview.
how: Zod schemas for manifest_version/dxt_version 0.1 to 0.4 define name, version, author, server {type: python|node|binary, entry_point, mcp_config {command,args,env,platform_overrides}}, tools, prompts, compatibility {claude_desktop, platforms (darwin, win32, linux), runtimes (python, node)}, user_config fields {type string|number|boolean|directory|file, title, description, required, default, multiple, sensitive, min, max}, icons, screenshots, localization and _meta. The Extensions service (24 methods) includes installDxt, installDxtUnpacked, installDxtFromDirectory, handleDxtFile, installExtensionFromPreview, getManifestCompatibilityResult, getInstalledExtensionsWithState, getIsUpdateAvailable, settings get/set and deleteExtension; staging directories dxt-staging, dxt-install-*, dxt-unpacked-* are used.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon supports installable connectors, adopt the MCPB manifest as-is for compatibility with the existing extension ecosystem.
notes: The MCPB spec page returned HTTP 503 during this pass; schema read from the bundled copy.

name: Extension trust: signature requirement, install-time allow/block check and continuous re-check
what: Admins can require signed extensions, enforce an allowlist, and block extensions by hash; already installed extensions are re-checked and disabled if they become blocked.
how: isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired (fail-closed true) and isDesktopExtensionEnabled are registry settings; at install a hash of the archive, manifest, signatureInfo and source are passed to checkCanInstall (returns canInstall/reason); extensions-blocklist.json stores downloaded blocklists; a re-check pass (checkAndDisableBlockedExtensions, trigger not traced) walks installed extensions and disables violations; unsigned installs fail with "This extension isn't signed. Ask your administrator ..."; the installed-extension metadata store (extensions-installations.json) self-heals from corrupt or malformed rows; auto-update is a separate setting (setIsDxtAutoUpdatesEnabled) with an Extensions Update Cache.
verevonRelevance: Verevon connector/extension governance should have the same three layers: signature policy, allow/block lists keyed by content hash, and re-evaluation of installed items when lists change.

name: Managed Python runtime for extensions via a pinned uv with checksum verification
what: Python-based extensions run with a downloaded, pinned uv binary (not the user's Python), verified by checksum and extracted safely.
how: ensureUvBinary looks for a system uv (verified with --version) and otherwise downloads uv 0.9.7 for the platform from GitHub releases with a pinned SHA-256 per platform (linux/darwin/win32 on x64/arm64) into userData/uv-runtime/uv-<ver>-<platform>-<arch>; downloads are resumable with streaming SHA-256, progress/ETA logs and a download-resume byte offset; archives are extracted (tar or zip) with a path-traversal guard ("Unsafe file path detected in archive"); registry egress requirements list the Python runtime hosts.
verevonRelevance: For sandboxed Python tools Verevon can pin uv by hash and manage it per app version; the resume-plus-hash download helper is reusable.

name: Artifacts: sandboxed HTML apps with an SRI-pinned CDN allow-list and a host tool bridge
what: Artifacts are HTML documents rendered in a locked-down partition that may only load approved libraries (with integrity hashes) and can call back into MCP tools or ask Claude through a narrow bridge.
how: The cowork-artifact scheme and a persist:cowork-artifact-<id> session host artifact pages; an allow-list of library URLs with sha384 SRI and usage hints (Chart.js 4.5.0, Grid.js 5.0.2 plus theme CSS, Mermaid 11.15.0 with securityLevel strict) is enforced by a webRequest filter (every request is cancelled unless it targets cowork-artifact:// or a listed URL) and by the per-page Content-Security-Policy script/style sources, and is exported as usage hints for the model (INF); the bridge (callMcpTool, askClaude, runScheduledTask, navigateHost, openExternalUrl, setEditableFocused) requires mcp__<server>__<tool> names resolved by the host (resolveMcpToolId), and settings gate write tools and scheduled-task runs from artifacts; artifact popups are adopted into separate windows with navigation and window.open blocked.
verevonRelevance: The artifact sandbox contract (approved libs with SRI, host-mediated tool calls, popups adopted into guarded windows) is a strong baseline for Verevon's chat/agent page artifacts.
notes: Whether the library list is exhaustive for the web-chat artifact viewer is unknown; this list is for Cowork local artifacts.

name: Built-in tool catalog governed by policy: 22 named tools including REPL, JavaScript and task tools
what: The engine's built-in tools are a closed, named set that admin policy can allow, ask about or block individually, with web tools treated specially for egress.

verevonRelevance: A concrete, short list to benchmark Verevon's own tool set against (note the presence of a JavaScript REPL tool, task-management tools and ToolSearch for deferred tool loading).

name: Cowork sandbox VM: per-OS hypervisor backends behind one TypeScript interface
what: Cowork runs the agent inside a Linux virtual machine on the user's computer: Hyper-V on Windows, Apple Virtualization on macOS, KVM on Linux, all driven through the same vm client API.
how: The vm object exposes configure, startVM(bundlePath, memoryGB, cpuCount, networkMode "gvisor", apiProbeURL, guestProxy, ipv6), stopVM, isRunning, isGuestConnected, refreshGuestProxy, spawn, kill, writeStdin, isProcessRunning, mountPath, readFile, getMemoryInfo, getSessionsDiskInfo, deleteSessionDirs, pruneSessionCaches, installSdk, runEdrExtension, addApprovedOauthToken, getNetworkDrives and event callbacks. On Windows the implementation is a privileged Go service reached over a named pipe; on macOS it is the Swift addon (@ant/claude-swift, logs swift.log and vzgvisor.log); Linux uses a helper configured with KVM and vhost-vsock (failure reasons kvm_permission_denied, vhost_vsock_module_missing). Unsupported hosts report typed reasons (hcs_not_available, virtualization_tools_missing, os_version_too_new, beta_disabled_by_org).
evidence: claude:tmp/claude-audit/eipc_services_v3.txt (scout parser output of the 89 eipc service definitions; cross-checked against ao() calls in index.chunk-EzXl5k4A.js~L45753-L45876)
verevonRelevance: The most important environment-control reference for Verevon sandboxes: a narrow, versioned VM RPC (start, spawn, mount, egress, event stream) that hides the hypervisor, so Rust can implement Hyper-V/KVM/Virtualization backends behind one trait.
notes: macOS gVisor usage is inferred from the vzgvisor.log name and the "gvisor" network mode parameter (INF, medium).

name: VM bundle manifest embedded in the app, with four retained versions and binary deltas
what: The sandbox image is downloaded on demand against a manifest baked into the app; updates can use binary deltas from recent versions instead of re-downloading about 1.2 GB.
how: vmBundleManifest has versions[0] as current plus three older shas kept so a publish workflow can compute deltas (publishedAt 2026-09-11, 2026-06-04, 2026-03-30, 2026-02-18). Files are keyed by OS (unix, win32) and arch (arm64, x64): rootfs.img (raw 10 GiB, about 1.2 to 1.3 GB compressed) on macOS/Linux, rootfs.vhdx plus vmlinuz and initrd on Windows, initrd-micro in the newest, each with checksum, size, rawChecksum, rawSize, progress ranges for a single progress bar and a deltas list {fromSha, checksum, size} (about 170 to 520 MB). The delta path (flag-gated) checks the installed sha file, prefers a local source when present, applies the delta with the native applyVmImageDelta and falls back to a full download.
verevonRelevance: Verevon sandbox images should follow the same discipline: manifest-pinned versions, checksums on compressed and raw forms, delta updates from N recent versions and a single progress range per bundle.
notes: Checksums are published in the bundle; no download was attempted.

name: Windows VM service architecture: Go service, named pipe, userspace gVisor networking and host CA injection
what: On Windows a separate privileged service starts the VM and provides its network, so the unprivileged desktop app never needs admin rights and all guest traffic is mediated by the host.
how: The Windows service "CoworkVMService" (cowork-svc.exe, Go 1.25) is started through the Service Control Manager by the app (queryWindowsServiceState/startWindowsService via the native addon with start backoff, denied/failed/timeout classification and a servicing guard) and listens on \\.\pipe\cowork-vm-service. Embedded Go packages show gvisor-tap-vsock (userspace network stack), linuxkit/virtsock (Hyper-V sockets), miekg/dns, tcpproxy, gopacket, dhcp, a Windows system-proxy reader (anthropics/win-httpproxy), HCN network init, per-session console pipes, disk-state probes and trusted-root enumeration (LoadTrustedCACertificates, certChainsToTrustedRoot). A VHDX tools disk smol-bin.<arch>.vhdx (37.7 MB) is copied into the bundle before boot.
evidence: claude:resources/cowork-svc.exe Go module/package strings (cowork-win32-service/vm, /pipe, /logsink; gvisor-tap-vsock; virtsock; win-httpproxy)
REA ev_f3c5370b120aaa7c8c8446818f8b81f6157f1a0bb8d5174bbbf507221869789c (inspect_pe_resources resources/cowork-svc.exe: PE32+ x64, 13605200 bytes, 0 resource entries)
verevonRelevance: The architecture to emulate for a Windows Verevon sandbox: privileged service + verified pipe + host-side userspace networking, so egress policy lives outside the guest.
notes: Package-level behaviour is inferred from symbol names; the binary was not executed. REA's PE tool confirms format only.

name: VM service RPC protocol: length-prefixed JSON, request ids, event subscription and guest-initiated calls
what: The desktop talks to the VM service with a tiny RPC: 4-byte big-endian length plus a JSON body, with correlation ids, a separate event connection and the ability for code in the guest to call back into the host.
how: Frames are {method,id,params} and {id,success,result|error}, capped at 10 MiB; the client retries idempotent calls once if the pipe closes, redials with backoff while the service starts, and tracks orphaned responses; events (stdout, stderr, exit with signal/oomKillCount/peakBytes, error, networkStatus, apiReachability, startupStep) arrive on a subscribeEvents connection; the guest can send {type:"request",id,method,params} which is routed to a registered handler and answered by sendGuestResponse. A configure call sends userDataName/userDataRoot (roaming vs local data location) and optional memory/cpu.
verevonRelevance: A concrete wire contract Verevon can copy for its own VM/sandbox agent: simple framing, id correlation, event stream and bidirectional RPC (guest-to-host) for credential or file brokering.

name: Process-in-VM model: named processes with mounts, egress allow-lists, one-shot runs and skeleton homes
what: Each agent process runs in the VM with its own working directory under /sessions/<id>, selected folder mounts (read-only or read-write, with hidden sub-paths), a per-process allowed-domain list and optional oneShot semantics.
how: spawn({id,name,command,args,isResume,cwd,env,additionalMounts,allowedDomains,oneShot,mountSkeletonHome,oauthToken}) returns failedMounts; mountPath(processId, subpath, mountName, mode, hide[]) adds mounts later; log categories show vm, hcs, hvsock, vnet, hcn, vhdx, console, hyperv, hidefs, tapvsock, timesync and skeletonfs layers; one-shot processes have spawn-ack timeouts derived from mount count and distinguish host_ack_timeout, host_timeout, guest_stall and guest_error; session directories can be pruned by free-space thresholds (getSessionsDiskInfo, pruneSessionCaches, deleteSessionDirs).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's sandbox API should include per-process mounts with hide lists, per-process egress lists and one-shot runs with explicit timeout classes.

name: VM startup state machine with typed failure causes and a bounded auto-reinstall policy
what: Starting the VM is a sequence of named steps with timing; failures are classified (download, boot, host share not mounted, connection timeout, VPN routing conflict, hypervisor errors) and the app decides whether to retry, show a fix, or reinstall the bundle once.
how: QGr runs download_and_sdk_prepare, load_swift_api, then startVM, then polls guest connectivity until a deadline, then sdk_install; vmStartupStep events from the service are merged; on failure it gathers VPN/network diagnostics and logs error_type (service_unavailable, vm_boot_error, vm_stopped, connection_timeout, host_share_not_mounted, vpn_routing_conflict); HCS errors map to sentinels such as HYPERVISOR_VIRT_DISABLED, VM_LOGON_RIGHT_DENIED, VHDX_ACCESS_DENIED, VHDX_COMPRESSED_OR_ENCRYPTED; auto-reinstall of the workspace is attempted at most once, and skipped for download failures, service failures, drive-share failures, user-requested restarts, hypervisor errors and disk-full.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's runner start flow should emit typed step events and map low-level hypervisor errors to user-fixable categories; the "reinstall once" guard avoids reinstall loops.

name: Host-mediated egress control: per-process allowed domains, wildcard stripping under compliance, guest proxy
what: Network access from the sandbox is limited to listed domains and flows through a host-side proxy; a compliance (HIPAA) gate removes the all-domains wildcard.
how: spawn() accepts allowedDomains; a wrapper (vxn/_xn) removes the "*" entry and re-adds the mandatory domain set when the HIPAA gate is active, logging lam_hipaa_gate_blocked(surface=vm_egress_allowlist); the VM start passes guestProxy and an API-reachability probe URL; refreshGuestProxy refreshes the guest proxy configuration on demand (returns an outcome or unsupported); settings expose coworkEgressAllowedHosts and probeEgressHosts; the Windows service also injects host-trusted root CAs for TLS-inspecting enterprise proxies and reads the system proxy.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs the same enforcement point: allowlists enforced by a host-side network stack, with tenant policy able to forbid wildcards.
notes: The proxy auto-config fetch for the VM is at L103169 (cowork-vm-pac-fetch); SOCKS proxies are not supported by the downstream HTTP agents (L36366).

name: Computer use executor profiles per OS: native filtering on macOS, window masking on Windows, none on Wayland
what: The computer-use tool adapts to what each OS can do: macOS can exclude windows from screenshots natively, Windows masks excluded windows, Linux/Wayland has no filtering and no hit-testing.
how: CU_SUPPORTED_PLATFORMS is darwin, win32, linux; capability profiles are {screenshotFiltering:"native",platform:"darwin"}, {screenshotFiltering:"mask",platform:"win32"}, {screenshotFiltering:"none",platform:"linux",hitTest:"none"}; minimum macOS 14 (app-scoped mode 15+, tested up to 26); Linux uses an xdg portal RemoteDesktop/Clipboard probe; tools are named computer and computer_batch with actions screenshot, zoom, left_click, right_click, double_click, left_click_drag, key, type, scroll, hover. Sub-gates default to pixelValidation off, clipboardPasteMultiline, mouseAnimation, hideBeforeAction, autoTargetDisplay, clipboardGuard, maskFailClosed and adaptiveResolution on, coordinate mode "pixels".
verevonRelevance: A Rust computer-use crate should expose the same capability struct (filtering mode, hit-test, min OS) so the Model Plane can tell the model what is and is not enforced.
notes: "chicago" is the internal codename for computer use (GrowthBook chicago_config).

name: Tiered per-app access for computer use: view-only browsers, click-only terminals, full for the rest
what: Apps are granted at a tier by category: browsers are view-only (use the Chrome tool instead), terminals and IDEs are click-only (use Bash instead), everything else is full control; the tier is enforced at call time by checking the frontmost app.
how: The tool description teaches the tiers; handleToolCall errors when a read-tier app is in front for left_click or a click-tier app is in front for type/right_click; request_access presents an approval dialog with the tier; open_application works at any tier; grants are per session and a user-maintained denied-apps list (chicagoUserDeniedBundleIds preference) excludes bundle ids. DOC confirms View only / Click only / Full control tiers and that approvals last for the session.
verevonRelevance: Directly reusable policy: classify target apps into read/click/full tiers and route the model to safer tools (browser MCP, shell) for the restricted categories.

name: Prompt-injection hardening of the installed-app list given to the model
what: The list of installed apps that is embedded in the computer-use tool description is sanitised so an attacker-named app cannot inject instructions.
how: Names are NFC-normalised, trimmed, limited to 40 characters and to a Unicode letter/digit/space/punctuation allow-list (regex), de-duplicated and sorted, then truncated to 200 entries with an "... and N more" line; enumeration has a timeout and is omitted if slow; running apps and home-folder apps are prioritised.
verevonRelevance: Any Verevon tool description that interpolates user-controlled strings (file names, app names, connector names) needs the same allow-list and length bounds.

name: Machine-wide computer-use lock, attended/unattended rules and turn-end restoration
what: Only one Claude session may drive the computer at a time; when a turn ends the app restores hidden windows and the user's clipboard.
how: A lock holder (vH CuLock with cuLockChanged events and a glow overlay) makes other sessions get "Another Claude session is currently using the computer ..."; chicagoAutoUnhide is a preference; at turn end/leaving-running the host auto-unhides apps it hid (cuHiddenDuringTurn) and restores the clipboard; unattended turns are denied approvals; hideBeforeAction hides other apps before acting.
verevonRelevance: For Verevon computer use add a global device lock and mandatory restoration steps; both prevent "two agents fighting over one mouse" and leaked UI state.

name: Background (app-scoped) computer use with raw input and the app_* tool family
what: On macOS 15+ the agent can control a specific app window in the background without taking over the user's foreground, using a separate app_* tool family.
how: appScoped is enabled when the GrowthBook sub-gate and minimum macOS major are met, passing supportsRawInput to the tool schema builder; permission handling has special cases (app_bring_to_current_space requires approval, app_screenshot and app_list_windows still work when unattended); preference chicagoPreferredMode is background or full_control; native cuAppUnderPoint, cuControlAtPoint and cuFocusedControl support accessibility-based targeting.
verevonRelevance: The "act on a window without stealing focus" mode is the differentiator for Verevon computer use on Windows (UI Automation/PostMessage routes) compared with whole-screen control.
notes: Windows support for app-scoped mode was not observed; the version gates are macOS.

name: Teach mode, watch-and-record and voiceover capture for learning from the user

how: Preloads computerUseTeach.js, computerUseWatchRecord.js and watchRecordChooser.js; eipc services CuTeach, CuWatchRecordChooser, CuWatchRecordPill; native exports watchRecorderStart/Subscribe/NowT and watchVoiceoverStart/Stop/SubscribePcm/ListInputDevices; frames and thumbnails are handled by copper-heron methods (take/finalize/discard); the teach overlay is tied to the computer-use tool schema via teachMode.

name: Framebuffer preview and live view of the controlled computer (RFB-capable client)

name: Claude in Chrome: native-messaging host, three transports and org gating
what: The agent can drive the user's own Chrome (or Edge, Brave, Chromium, Prisma, Island) through an extension; the desktop registers a native host, talks to the extension over a verified local pipe or through a cloud relay, and can disable the whole surface by org policy.

name: Browser-pane and preview sandboxing: jitless mode, denied permissions, origin allow-lists
what: Pages the agent previews or browses in-app run in isolated sessions with no permissions, optional JIT-disabled JavaScript, and origin approval prompts for sensitive hosts.
how: Preview webviews are created with session partitions, sandbox true, contextIsolation true, focusOnNavigation false, disableDialogs true for non-Claude pages, plugins controlled, and additionalArguments --js-flags=--jitless when the jitless setting is on; file-preview and artifact sessions install setPermissionRequestHandler(deny) and setPermissionCheckHandler(false) and a webRequest filter that cancels everything except the app scheme and the PDF viewer extension; a Claude page preview has its own preload (claudePagePreview.js); launch preview keeps allowed origins/domain transitions in main-only preferences.
verevonRelevance: The "preview untrusted HTML/web in the agent UI" surface in Verevon should adopt permission-deny sessions and optional JIT-off rendering.

name: Terminal host with a disk-backed scrollback flight recorder, secret redaction and shell fallback
what: Terminal sessions run in a utility process; their output is also written to a size-bounded, redacted log so the agent (or the UI) can search or page back through scrollback after the fact.
how: ptyHostWorker spawns node-pty ptys (cols/rows/cwd/env) and posts spawned/data/exit/spawn-error; if the primary shell fails to start or exits before output it swaps to a fallback executable (windowsFallbackFile), posts spawn-fallback and replays typed input. A scrollback writer tracks ANSI/VT parser state so segment rotation never splits an escape sequence, applies streaming secret redactors that replace a given secret with * across chunk boundaries, writes mode-0600 segment files (max 16 segments of 4M characters, 4 MiB backlog, gap marker "[... earlier output not kept ...]") and answers read-scrollback requests by line window or grep (max matches).
verevonRelevance: A "terminal flight recorder" with redaction is what makes agent terminals inspectable without dumping secrets into context; port it as a Rust crate (vte parser plus segmented log).
notes: node-pty is optional and unpacked; on Windows it uses ConPTY.

name: Git safety harness: allow-listed subcommands, hardened config and private indexes
what: Every git command the desktop runs on behalf of the agent or UI goes through a policy layer that limits subcommands and flags and neutralises repository-controlled code execution.
how: The git context builder sets GIT_DIR, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_WORK_TREE and a private GIT_INDEX_FILE under Desktop's index directory, refuses a relative GIT_DIR or an index outside the private directory, verifies that the git binary honours the shadow layout (self-check refs/git-dir/common-dir), and passes hardening options: core.hooksPath=NUL, core.fsmonitor=, safe.bareRepository=explicit, core.useReplaceRefs=false, core.commitGraph=false, gc.auto=0, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM and a controlled GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL; a strict subcommand/flag allow-list covers read-tree, update-ref, symbolic-ref, update-index, diff/log/show/status, remote get-url, branch, hash-object (no -w), cat-file, clean, checkout, merge, commit and rm with per-flag checks.
verevonRelevance: Any Verevon feature that runs git inside untrusted repositories (worktree creation, PR tooling, checkpoints) should use this posture instead of raw git calls; hooks/fsmonitor are the classic code-execution vectors.
notes: Located in index.chunk-C5LEPGle.js and the heavy-work worker; the exact set of "postures" (hydrate etc.) was not enumerated.

name: Worktrees, branch switching and PR tooling as first-class host services
what: Sessions can run in isolated git worktrees, branch switches stash or WIP-commit safely, and PR operations (review comments, checks, merge, auto-fix) are exposed as host calls.
how: GitWorktreeManager keeps a pool in git-worktrees.json (defaults: ccMaxWarmWorktrees 3 pre-created worktrees, ccBranchPrefix "claude", ccWorktreeReapAfterHours 24; a corrupt JSON file is renamed aside as git-worktrees.json.corrupt-<time> and the pool restarts empty); LocalSessions methods include getGitInfo, getLocalBranches, stashWorkingTree, commitWipForBranchSwitch, discardWorkingTree, checkBranchSwitchConflict, discardKeptWorktree, getPrChecks, getPrOverview, createPrReviewComment, resolvePrReviewThread, submitPrReview, mergePr, enableAutoMerge, setBoundPrAutoFix and an auto-archive-on-PR-close option; folderWorktrees flags (local and remote).

name: Credential-bearing path classifier that blocks folder grants and mounts
what: The app refuses to grant or mount folders that hold credentials or browser profiles (for example .ssh, .aws, .kube, gcloud, gh, browser LevelDB/IndexedDB), including through alias tricks.
how: A normaliser lowercases path segments and rejects: NTFS alternate data streams and drive-colon forms, 8.3 short-name suffixes (~N), a .vol or proc root, and chezmoi-style source names (dot_, private_, encrypted_ prefixes mapped back to dotfiles); then a deny list matches segment names (.ssh, .aws, .azure, .kube, .gnupg, .docker, .claude, .terraform.d, microsoft edge) and multi-segment paths (gcloud, gh, 1Password CLI, cargo/composer/maven/gem credentials, huggingface token, rclone, sops, ngrok, pulumi, stripe, doctl, fly, wrangler, glab, circleci, snowsql, github-copilot hosts, .codex/auth.json, local storage/leveldb, session storage, indexeddb ...) and file-name prefixes/suffixes and kubeconfig.
verevonRelevance: Copy the list and the alias-normalisation rules into Verevon's Data/Model plane folder-grant validator; it encodes years of "where secrets live" knowledge.
notes: The full lists are longer than recorded here; this is a refusal list for grants, not a read blocker for already granted folders (INF).

name: Real-user-gesture gating for privileged native actions
what: Native actions triggered from web content (such as always-allow dialogs or opening external apps) only proceed shortly after a genuine mouse click or activation key, so scripted pages cannot trigger them silently.
how: A per-webContents tracker listens to before-input-event and input-event, records the last primary mouse up, activation key (Enter/Space) and digit-key times (ignoring right/middle buttons and auto-repeat and allowing suppressors), and exposes helpers (bMn/yM/xMn) that return true only if the gesture is within about 1.5 s (mouse down to up within 5 s); sensitive handlers call them before showing consent or acting.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's native bridge should require a recent trusted input event for approval-sensitive calls; this blocks a class of prompt-injection-to-action chains.

name: Consent copy for spoofable local-network hosts
what: When the agent's browser tools want to always allow a host whose name only exists on the local network, the dialog explains that another network could reuse the same name and address.
how: SMn builds a question dialog "Always allow reads on {host}?" or "Always allow Claude on {host}?" with detail text about café Wi-Fi spoofing and offers Always allow / Allow once or Cancel, supporting host families with ports.
verevonRelevance: Small but valuable UX/security detail for Verevon browser grants: treat private-name hosts differently from public hosts.

name: Dangerous file-type list guarding "open with default app" and downloads
what: Files the agent produces or fetches are not opened automatically if their extension can execute code or install software.
how: Two lists enumerate executable/script/installer extensions (.exe, .msi, .appinstaller, .scr, .hta, .ps1, .vbs, .lnk, .desktop, .app, .command, .terminal, .fileloc, .scpt, .workflow, .mobileconfig and many more) used by the open/download helpers.
verevonRelevance: Reuse as a deny-by-default list in the Verevon artifact "open locally" action.

name: VM heartbeat monitor: 30-second pings, five-strike restart and guest-disconnect detection
what: While the sandbox is up the app pings the guest regularly and restarts the VM automatically if it stops answering, distinguishing a dead guest from a stopped VM.
how: After sdk_install the host starts a heartbeat (flag-gated, fallback monitor otherwise): every 30 s it checks isGuestConnected and calls isProcessRunning("__heartbeat__") with a 15 s timeout; a guest that was connected and then disconnects counts as a failure; five consecutive failures (SG=5) or a vmStopped event with an error trigger lam_vm_heartbeat_failure and a joined restart ("heartbeat_failure" reason). Failure counters reset on a successful ping.
verevonRelevance: A simple, proven liveness contract for Verevon runners: ping a sentinel process, count consecutive failures, restart through one joined path.

name: Host-side egress proxy with TLS interception hints and out-of-band token handoff
what: Traffic from the sandbox passes through a host proxy whose logs mention intercepted TLS, and the API token is handed to the VM service separately from the agent environment.
how: Error-line patterns include "Cannot read TLS response from mitm'd server", "Cannot write TLS response body from mitm'd client" and "[proxy] <<< UPSTREAM ERROR:"; the spawn call takes an oauthToken parameter after the token is deleted from env, and a service RPC addApprovedOauthToken(token) exists; trusted root CAs from the host are enumerated by the service (LoadTrustedCACertificates).
verevonRelevance: If Verevon needs policy-enforced egress from sandboxes it will likely need TLS interception with a guest-trusted CA and credential injection at the proxy so tokens never enter the guest; this is strong evidence that Anthropic does so (INF).
notes: That the proxy injects credentials is an inference from the RPC names and log strings; it was not observed.

name: Device as tool host for cloud sessions: remote-tools registration, tool announcements and bridge RPC
what: The desktop can act as a "device" whose tools (computer use, browser, file access, bash when allowed, direct MCP inventory) are advertised to cloud sessions, so a session started on claude.ai or a phone can operate this computer.
how: A remote-tools module exposes getRemoteToolsComputerToolNames, getRemoteToolsBrowserToolNames, getRemoteToolsFileToolNames, getRemoteToolsDirectMcpInventory, publishDeviceToolAnnouncement (file tool names, folder access mode, delete permission), initRemoteToolsDeviceIfGated, reloadRemoteToolsDevice, closeRemoteToolsDevice, device bash availability and per-kind RPC deadlines (device_bash, device_stage_files, device_commit_files); a BridgeTransport carries calls, a createDeviceOAuthTokenProvider mints device tokens, remote computer-use sessions keep allowed apps and selected display (getRemoteCuAllowedApps/SelectedDisplayId) and can release the machine lock; an MCP server named cowork-device-dispatch with listChanged exposes device tools; the device name derives from the hostname plus profile suffix; preference remoteToolsDeviceName and the computer-use toggle trigger re-announcement.
verevonRelevance: The model for Verevon "agent in the cloud, hands on the user's device": a signed device registers, announces tool sets and per-session grants, and cloud runs call it over a bridge with explicit deadlines per tool class.
notes: Only the export list, announcement function and constants were read; the bridge wire format was not decoded.

name: System-wide "write at cursor" assistant with per-app window-read consent (codename sableOtter)
what: A global hotkey opens a small overlay where the user dictates or types an instruction; Claude can read the focused field, selection, clipboard and (with consent) the visible window text, then types the result back into the app.
how: A Windows module (initSableOtterWin32) uses a native probe to classify the focused control and refuses secure fields, terminals, always-excluded and user-excluded apps, non-text fields and oversize selections ("Claude doesn't type into this app", "Not here: this is a secure field"); window/page/frame reading asks "Let Claude read this window first?" with once/always/never choices stored per app (preference sableOtterWindowApps may only lose entries when changed from the renderer); the request sent to the model carries sourceKind, source text, instruction, app class, clipboard text/image and window title/text; results are applied by pasting. A transparent always-on-top HUD window hosts the composer.
verevonRelevance: A system-wide inline writing assistant is a distinctive surface; if Verevon wants one, the consent-per-app model and refusal list (secure fields, terminals) are the template.
notes: Flag sableOtter was "unavailable" in the build defaults seen by the scout, so it may be off for most users.

name: Signed remote model catalog with capability metadata, hosted default and custom URL
what: Model availability and limits (context size, output size, effort levels, capabilities, knowledge cutoff, per-surface scope) come from a signed catalog the app fetches, so new models appear without an app update.
how: The default catalog is https://downloads.claude.ai/model-catalog/v1/catalog.json with a .raw-sig.json signature sidecar (size caps 2 MiB for the catalog, 16 KiB for the sidecar, 10 s timeout); managed config can disable it (models.catalogEnabled), point to a custom URL (validated; some hostnames are rejected as invalid) or mark it invalid/pending; entries are normalised field by field (max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens, effort_levels, default_effort, capabilities, family, knowledge_cutoff, defaults per surface cowork/code/chat); related registry keys are modelDiscoveryEnabled, inferenceModels, modelPrefer1mContext, defaultModelEffort, alwaysStartWithDefaultModel, advisorModel.

name: Layered diagnostics: component logs, VM guest logs, scrubbed support bundle, heap and memory traces
what: Support and developers can export a scrubbed bundle with app, VM, service, Chrome-host and MCP logs, take heap snapshots and record memory traces from the menu.
how: Log collectors enumerate main-process, main-view, MCP, Claude Code diagnostics, setup-window, Cowork VM (node, service, guest, swift, vzgvisor, coworkd) and chrome-native-host/app-cu-helper logs with per-source scrubbing (scrubBufferForBundle) and a SupportBundle service reporting stages; menu entries write a main-process heap snapshot to logs/traces and run a contentTracing memory trace (default 3 minutes, categories memory-infra, v8, blink.user_timing); a log-retention sweep is initialised at startup (L164988).

name: Customer-owned OpenTelemetry export from the app and the VM sandbox
what: Enterprises can send traces and metrics from the app, and from agent processes inside the VM, to their own collector with custom headers, auth mode and content-capture controls.
how: Registry keys otlpEndpoint, otlpProtocol (default http/protobuf), otlpHeaders, otlpHeadersHelper, otlpTracesEnabled, otlpAuthMode, otlpResourceAttributes and otlpContentCapture feed a per-spawn OTLP configuration (target vm, sandboxed, orgOtlpContentCapture, keptWarmBetweenTurns, platformLacksGrpcCaBridge) and an [otlp-collector-headers] helper refreshes headers; a guard forbids a console exporter; trace context is propagated into the engine environment as TRACEPARENT/TRACESTATE.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's enterprise observability story needs the same: customer OTLP targets, header helpers and content-capture categories, including from inside sandboxes.

name: Telemetry vocabulary and feature-exposure events for rollouts
what: Product behaviour is measured through a typed event vocabulary (lam_*, desktop_*, cu_*), plus experiment and exposure events so rollouts can be analysed.
how: Events such as lam_vm_startup_step, lam_vm_startup_failed, lam_vm_process_spawned, lam_escalated_tool_ask, lam_hipaa_gate_blocked, desktop_ccd_auto_update_check, desktop_ssh_process_reattached, cu_setting_changed and desktop_feature_exposure are logged with structured fields; GrowthbookExperimentEvent records experiment key and variation id once per session.
verevonRelevance: Define a closed event schema for Verevon runs (start step, failure class, approval outcome, gate blocks) early; it pays for itself in rollout debugging.

name: Main-process and renderer memory observability built into telemetry
what: Memory pressure is tracked for the main process, renderers, GPU and the VM guest and attached to events so leaks and low-memory failures can be found.
how: A metrics snapshot (app.getAppMetrics, process.memoryUsage, V8 heap limit) is cached and summarised into process_main_rss/heap/external and renderer RSS sums; renderer heap/Blink bytes arrive through RendererMemoryReporter; VM memory (total/free/available/min available) and host availability are attached to VM events; a native readOwnMemoryComposition/readProcessFootprints supports Windows footprints.

name: Compliance gates that disable surfaces and strip wildcards for HIPAA-regulated organisations
what: When an organisation is HIPAA-restricted, whole features (Cowork browser, Chrome extension, computer use, wildcard VM egress) are turned off or narrowed, and telemetry is re-scrubbed.
how: A coworkHipaaRestricted preference and org flags feed gate objects (Pj("claude_browser_extension"), Pj("cowork_browser_pane")) that return a block reason, log lam_hipaa_gate_blocked(surface), invalidate prompts when policy changes, deny computer use with a fixed message and drop "*" from VM egress; telemetry events call rescrub(originOrgId) for HIPAA orgs.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Zero-Data-Retention and compliance flags should be modelled the same way: named gates per surface, reason codes, and automatic prompt rebuild when policy flips.

name: Navigation, popup and protocol guards for every web surface
what: Web content cannot navigate the privileged views to arbitrary origins, open arbitrary windows or launch external protocols without checks.
how: will-navigate/will-redirect/will-frame-navigate/will-attach-webview are intercepted per view (main view allows only app/claude origins, popups block all navigation and non-about/data/blob frames), setWindowOpenHandler routes through allow-list helpers (AI/_Yn/RI) and returns deny; did-create-window verifies the opener is the main frame, destroys unexpected windows (including unexpected /code children) and wraps show/hide/minimize to track focus; artifact protocol links require consent and a setting "Always allow {protocol} links from artifacts".

name: Prompt-injection posture in host-written instructions: link safety and untrusted-content rules
what: The computer-use instructions tell the model to treat links in emails/messages as suspicious, never click web links with computer-use tools and use the browser tool instead.
how: The system-prompt segment appended for computer use includes link-safety rules and the tiered-app guidance; deny messages are written to steer behaviour; the app list is sanitised; forged card-name tool asks are denied.

name: Fail-closed defaults and egress declarations on every managed key
what: Unreadable or malformed enterprise config never silently loosens security: keys declare their fail-closed value and the network hosts they need.
how: In the registry, failClosedValue (for example signature required true, extensions enabled false) applies when a key cannot be read; legacy key renames explain the effect of an old name being unreadable; egressRequirements functions compute required hosts from a setting value (extensions need the Python runtime hosts); managed-tier problems disable local settings entirely and are surfaced.
verevonRelevance: Make fail-closed values and required egress hosts part of the Verevon policy schema so admins can derive firewall allow-lists automatically.

name: Sentry and hook isolation: telemetry code can never crash the app
what: Crash-reporting callbacks are wrapped so an exception inside a hook drops or passes the event and logs once, instead of breaking the app.
how: R6 wraps Sentry hooks (beforeSend-style) with try/catch and promise rejection handling, logging the first failure per hook and choosing "keep" or drop semantics; Sentry release and debug ids are injected into every build file.
verevonRelevance: Wrap all observability callbacks in isolation guards in the Rust shell.

name: Folder grants as first-class state: per-session, routine and remote-chat grants with consent memory
what: Which folders the agent may touch is tracked in several grant stores that only the main process can modify, and every grant records how and when it was consented.
how: Main-only preference keys include remoteSessionFolderGrants, routineFolderGrants, remoteChatFolderGrants, remoteChatFolderAccessReports, remoteFolderConsentMemory, remoteFolderConsentFromSettings, localAgentModeTrustedFolders, folderTccProbeResults and coworkLegacyRootGrantsPruned; a one-time migration prunes legacy never-served grants at startup; eipc services grant/revoke routine folders and project-upload folders, check and save trust per folder, and macOS TCC probes classify protected folders; folder paths are screened by the credential-path classifier before grant.

verevonRelevance: Verevon should treat grants as explicit, auditable records (who, when, scope: session/routine/remote) editable only by trusted code.

name: Deep-link hardening: route normalisation, id validation, duplicate suppression and admin kill switches
what: claude:// links cannot be used to escape their route, replay a login, or sign into a connector when the admin has turned that off.
how: The URL handler resolves each link against its expected route and warns "normalized outside its route" if path normalisation leaves the route (MCP auth callback, epitaxy), validates conversation/project ids with a pattern before navigating, suppresses repeat login callbacks (desktop_login_callback_duplicate_suppressed), sets the cross-domain anonymous-id cookie only for SSO callbacks, honours disableConnectorSignInInApp for step=finish connector links, and offers a setting to disable deep-link handling entirely.
verevonRelevance: Deep links are an injection surface for desktop agents; validate ids, normalise paths and make links idempotent as done here.

name: Host-side path confinement hook for file tools: protected-location carve-outs and alternate-spelling rejection
what: File tools in host-loop sessions are checked before they run: paths must be absolute and inside the session's connected folders, symlinks are resolved safely, and protected locations (system, credential, Claude-internal data) are carved out even inside granted folders.
how: A PreToolUse hook (matcher on file tools plus MultiEdit) calls a gate that rejects root- or drive-relative paths and Windows alternate spellings (stream names, 8.3 short names, device prefixes, trailing dot or space), resolves the path with a safe resolver against the allowed roots, computes grant carve-outs and user-revoked grants, blocks writes or reads that land in a carved protected location, blocks search tools whose root contains a protected location, and applies per-tool judgement (writable roots, host-executed roots); every block returns an explanatory reason so the model can adapt, and gate errors fail closed with a retry message. A separate PreToolUse hook validates the Artifact tool path. Additional disallowedTools are generated from the connected-folder carve-outs.
verevonRelevance: The most concrete file-confinement design seen: pair a credential-path classifier with a PreToolUse hook that resolves symlinks and carves protected paths out of granted folders; port it to Rust with capability opens and mirror the explanatory block messages.
notes: HostLoop is the default host-native mode: the agent loop and file tools run on the host with path-based access control while shell commands run in the VM (registry warning text at core L20652); requireCoworkFullVmSandbox moves the whole loop into the VM.

name: Tool-call policy as code: CEL rules plus an external decision endpoint (unreleased)
what: Admins will be able to govern every tool call with up to 100 Common Expression Language rules or by delegating to their own HTTPS policy service, failing closed when rules cannot be read.
how: Registry keys toolPolicyRules and toolPolicyEndpoint (scope 3p, availableInVersion "@next", public-undocumented, appliesOffDeviceOnly, beta key selfHostedSessions, remote-only and hot-applied) define: cel_env_version (integer), rules [{id (lowercase slug, unique), condition (CEL, 1-4096 chars), action allow|deny|require_approval, reason (required unless allow, 300 chars)}] with order-independent semantics where any deny wins; a fail-closed stand-in rule "unreadable-rule-set" (condition true, action deny); and an endpoint object {url (https, loopback, query and fragment rejected), credentialKind anonymous|credentialHelper, credentialHelper, onFailure deny|allow (default deny), timeoutSec 1-10 (default 5)}.
verevonRelevance: Directly relevant to Verevon's Control Plane: ship tool policy as CEL rules with deny-wins semantics plus an optional external PDP webhook with explicit failure mode and timeout; both fail closed by default.
notes: Unreleased ("@next") schema only; the evaluator and the CEL environment (variables exposed to conditions) were not found in this bundle, so evaluation likely lives in the engine or server.

name: Versioned policy schema with migrations, per-tool MCP permissions and fail-closed built-in tool policy
what: Policy keys evolve safely: each is tagged with the app versions that read it and the products that consume it, old shapes are rewritten with a stated effect, and unknown permissions become blocked.
how: Managed MCP servers carry a per-tool toolPolicy; the array form [{serverName,tools:[{toolName,permission}]}] is read by desktop 1.15200.0 and later (older desktops enforce no blocks), a malformed record fails closed (all plugin-delivered MCP tools blocked), the value "ask-session" is rewritten to "ask" for older readers and an unrecognised permission is treated as blocked; builtinToolPolicy (values include ask-session from 1.40609.0) fails closed to "ask" for every built-in tool; entries have readers ["desktop","m365","code"], support scopes and availableInVersion, deprecations with rewrite functions and checkDropped hooks; egressRequirements for managed MCP servers derive hosts from URL and OAuth settings (for example login.microsoftonline.com).
verevonRelevance: Verevon policy documents need a version and reader matrix like this so a tenant's policy cannot silently weaken when an older client reads it.

name: Workspace confinement and sandbox toggles: allowed folders, block reads outside working directory, strict mode
what: Admins and users can restrict which folders sessions may use, block reads outside the working directory, and turn the Claude Code OS sandbox and its strict mode on; some API errors are mapped to a strict-sandbox explanation.
how: Registry keys allowedWorkspaceFolders and blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories (public-undocumented) and the ClaudeCode service methods setLocalSandboxEnabled, setStrictSandboxMode and getLocalSandboxStatus; error classification maps "requires strict Claude Code sandboxing" 400 responses to a dedicated category; quickWriteEnabled and hardwareBuddyEnabled show the same per-feature switch pattern with fail-closed values.
verevonRelevance: Model these as tenant-level toggles in Verevon (workspace allow-list, read confinement, strict sandbox) and surface a specific error when a run is refused by them.
notes: The Linux sandbox itself (bubblewrap strings appear in the CLI) was not inspected.

name: Nonce-bound consent for agent self-management tools (rename session, start side session, bind PR)
what: When the agent asks to rename its session, open a side session or bind a pull request, the host interposes a consent step whose approval is cryptographically tied to the exact content shown, and some abusive requests are denied outright.
how: A session broker implements PreToolUse hook outputs: setSessionTitleConsent denies self-rename by subagents ("subagent_self_rename"), titles with hidden/invisible text ("title_hidden_text") and failed target lookups, otherwise mints a consent nonce for (session, target, previous title) and returns permissionDecision "ask" with updatedInput carrying the nonce (or silently updates input when the stand-down policy is bypass); redeemBindPrConsent(session,url,nonce) consumes a one-time consent for binding a PR; sideSessionStartConsent allows proposal/offer cards because they start nothing until the user presses them; denials are counted as desktop_ccd_permission_auto_denied with a reason.
verevonRelevance: Verevon approvals for agent-initiated metadata changes (titles, plan edits, memory writes) should bind consent to a nonce over the exact payload, deny invisible-text payloads, and be single-use; this closes consent-then-swap attacks.
notes: Semantics of the "stand down" policy and cause codes were not traced.

name: Hidden-title-bar window with a local title-bar page, themed overlay and display-aware placement
what: The window looks native but is custom: the title bar region is a local page, the OS caption buttons are themed via titleBarOverlay, and window position is restored onto a display that still exists.
how: BrowserWindow options use titleBarStyle hidden, titleBarOverlay true with color/symbolColor updated from a JSON message per main window or popout, trafficLightPosition on macOS, backgroundColor from nativeTheme (light/dark palettes), minWidth 600/minHeight 400, and placeOnDisplays/electron-window-state to restore bounds; the user's theme mode (system/light/dark) is applied to nativeTheme.themeSource; resize is debounced and re-lays out the child view.
verevonRelevance: Standard craft for the Verevon desktop shell; the title-bar-as-local-page trick keeps window controls working when the remote UI is loading or offline.

name: Close-to-tray, login startup and keep-reachable behaviour
what: Closing the window hides the app to the tray/menu bar (unless disabled) so background work and remote requests continue; the app can start at login in the background.
how: The main window close handler prevents default and either quits (when the tray/menu-bar preference is off) or hides the window (leaving fullscreen first); Startup service toggles login-item settings with a --startup argument (MSIX uses the exe path directly); background launches avoid showing the window (os_login/background_launch).

name: Quick Entry: global-shortcut mini window with dictation and recent chats

how: QuickWindow service (requestDismiss, requestDismissWithPayload with text/chatId/images, requestSkooch for size), a quick_window renderer, GlobalShortcut service (setGlobalShortcut validated for Electron accelerators), flags nativeQuickEntry/quickEntryGlobalShortcut/quickEntryDictation and QuickEntry.setRecentChats; on Windows a legacy path registers the shortcut when the main window is focused or hidden.

name: Three-layer Electron shell: privileged main, local chrome windows, and a remote-UI WebContentsView
what: The desktop app is a thin native shell. A local BrowserWindow draws the title bar and window chrome, while the actual Chat/Code/Cowork UI is the claude.ai web app loaded into a child WebContentsView that fills the window.
how: Main entry is .vite/build/index.pre.js (compile-cache hook, Sentry bootstrap) which requires the chunk graph. createMainWindow builds a BrowserWindow with preload mainWindow.js (local title-bar page, titleBarOverlay, hidden title bar) and then a second view with preload mainView.js; the view is attached with p.contentView.addChildView(y) and resized to the window content bounds on show/focus/resize. The window holds only IPC glue (titleBarReady, requestReloadMainView, requestRestartApp, requestMainMenuPopup); product UI is remote. Popouts are further BrowserWindows adopted from window.open of the main view.
evidence: REA ev_ad009afc4495e7b69f7e22b6972460adddac00cd2353e0dffe449d0da4bea7c8 (analyze_javascript_application summary of main/preload/worker subset: context_bridge_apis 52, IPC operations 1504 of which 9 literal and 1495 dynamic, renderer_transmissions 1278, renderer_listeners 226, semantic coverage partial)
