name: Hardened renderer baseline applied to every window
what: Every local window and embedded web surface runs with the sandbox on, context isolation on, node integration off and webview tags disabled, so a compromised page cannot reach Node or the file system directly.

Other window factories repeat sandbox:true/contextIsolation:true/nodeIntegration:false (design window, cowork artifact window, file preview, claude page preview, find-in-page, quick, about). Untrusted preview contents additionally get --js-flags=--jitless.
verevonRelevance: Adopt the same frozen baseline as a typed constant in the Verevon shell and refuse to construct a window without it; jitless preview content is a cheap extra for rendering model-authored HTML.
notes: Fuse configuration (@electron/fuses) is a build-time dev dependency; its runtime state was not observed.

name: Thirteen preload entry points, one per window role, each exposing a narrow surface
what: Each window role (main chrome, remote UI view, quick entry, about, find-in-page, buddy, design, page preview, cowork artifact, computer-use teach overlay, watch-record chooser, local-exec consent) has its own preload script so that only the role that needs a capability receives it.

name: Typed IPC runtime (eipc) with schema-validated arguments, results, stores and events
what: All renderer-to-main calls go through one generated, typed IPC layer. Every method validates its arguments and its return value, so a web page cannot send malformed data into native code.
how: ao(prefix,name,senderValidator,{methods,stores,events}) registers ipcMain.handle (or ipc.on for sync methods) on channel "$eipc_message$_<uuid>_$_<namespace>_$_<Service>_$_<method>". Each method entry is [name,[[argName,validator]...],resultValidator,'sync'?]; arguments are checked by Nxe, results by the result validator, and failures throw named errors ("failed to pass validation", "did not pass origin validation"). Events are dispatcher functions that call webContents.send with validated payloads. @ant/ipc-codegen (devDependency) generates the typed client; a second UUID (fcb91d11-...) isolates the window-manager library.
evidence: REA ev_ad009afc4495e7b69f7e22b6972460adddac00cd2353e0dffe449d0da4bea7c8 (analyze_javascript_application summary of main/preload/worker subset: context_bridge_apis 52, IPC operations 1504 of which 9 literal and 1495 dynamic, renderer_transmissions 1278, renderer_listeners 226, semantic coverage partial)
verevonRelevance: The strongest reusable pattern for the Verevon gateway: define each native/Model-Plane-facing method once with argument and result schemas, generate both the Rust handler trait and the TypeScript client, and reject on validation failure at the boundary.
notes: The generator role of @ant/ipc-codegen is inferred from its name and position in devDependencies; the runtime shape of the services is directly observed. In a Rust port this maps to serde-validated command structs (or specta/ts-rs generated TypeScript) plus a per-service sender policy. REA could only see 9 literal channels of 1504 IPC operations because the rest are string-concatenated.

name: Sender-origin allowlist enforced twice: in the preload and in the main process
what: Native services only answer the real claude.ai (or local app://) top-level page; a child iframe or a foreign origin gets an error even if it somehow reaches the IPC channel.
how: Main side validators (Xh and siblings) require senderFrame.parent===null and an origin of https://claude.ai, https://preview.claude.ai, https://claude.com, https://preview.claude.com or app://localhost (plus localhost and *.ant.dev only when a developer override flag is on). The preload repeats the check before it attaches each service object (webFrame.top equality plus the origin allowlist), and some services (AboutWindow, QuickWindow, MainWindowTitleBar) accept only parent===null. A separate allowed-origins constant (__ELECTRON_WINDOW_ALLOWED_ORIGINS__) guards the window-manager bridge.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's frontend/gateway should bind capability objects to an origin and top-frame check in both the preload analogue and the Rust handler; never rely on only one side.
notes: The scout's REA full-app run reported 63 sender_validation_observations; the subset run in this pass reported 0 because the validators live in the large core chunk.

name: Reactive store pattern layered on IPC (getState, getStateSync, push updates)
what: The UI can read shared native state (updater state, usage previews, spaces, support-bundle progress) and receive pushes when it changes, instead of polling.
how: Each service can declare stores: the runtime registers "<channel>_$store$_getState" (async) and "_$store$_getStateSync" handlers, validated against a store schema, and the main side obtains an update<Store>Store(state) function that validates and webContents.send()s on "<channel>_$store$_update". Events and stores share the validator machinery.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane sessions/runs could expose the same get-initial + push-update shape to the gateway for run status, cost and approvals so the UI never polls.

name: Namespaced capability objects injected into the page, conditional on origin
what: The web UI sees native features as window["claude.web"].LocalSessions.*, window["claude.settings"].MCP.*, window.electron_window.WindowManager.*, so features are grouped, discoverable and individually gated.
how: Preload helper functions (one per service) check the current page origin and top frame, then assign e["claude.web"][Service]=impl on a plain object; the object is exposed with contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld per top-level namespace. Namespaces seen: claude.web (about 55 services), claude.settings (about 17), claude.simulator, claude.internal.*, claude.buddy, claude.engineSurface, claude.officeAddin, claude.coworkArtifact, claude.designPdf, claude.telemetry, claude.hybrid, claude.skills, plus electron_window.WindowManager. Extra non-namespaced bridges: process, desktopBootFeatures, desktopManagedConfig, desktopEnterpriseConfig, desktopTelemetryConfig, desktopDeviceClass, desktopPreferredLanguages, electronIntl, electronWindowControl, claudeAppSettings, claudeAppBindings.

verevonRelevance: Use the same grouping (web, settings, internal) when designing the Verevon native bridge so capabilities can be granted per origin and audited per namespace.

name: 89 native service definitions, dominated by two giant session services
what: The renderer's native API is large: 89 services in 13 namespaces. LocalSessions alone has 321 methods and LocalAgentModeSessions 115, followed by Launch (86), Simulator (49), Custom3pSetup (35) and CoworkSpaces (33).
how: Scout parser output enumerates every ao() definition with method names; a cross-check shows ao() calls for ChromeExtension, ComputerUseTcc, FramebufferPreview, CoworkMemory, Launch, LocalSessions and ClaudeVM adjacent at L45801-L45876 of the core chunk. Method families include rewind/fork/steer/queue, git/PR tooling, SSH, scheduled tasks, plugins, VM and computer-use consent.
evidence: claude:tmp/claude-audit/eipc_services_v3.txt (scout parser output of the 89 eipc service definitions; cross-checked against ao() calls in index.chunk-EzXl5k4A.js~L45753-L45876)

name: Boot-time configuration injected through webPreferences.additionalArguments
what: The renderer gets feature availability and managed-config data synchronously at load, so the first paint already knows what is enabled without a round trip.
how: The main process serialises KV() (the feature table: 122 keys, each {status:...}) into "--desktop-features=<JSON>" and passes managed/enterprise config as another prefixed argument; the preload parses process.argv and exposes desktopBootFeatures, desktopManagedConfig, desktopEnterpriseConfig, desktopTelemetryConfig, desktopDeviceClass and desktopPreferredLanguages.
verevonRelevance: Verevon can bootstrap the SolidJS app with a signed-in capability/feature blob in the first HTML response instead of a flash-of-unconfigured UI.

name: MessagePort side channels for high-volume or streaming data
what: Large or streaming payloads (transcripts, framebuffer frames, artifact host tools, MCP traffic) bypass the request/response IPC and travel over transferred MessagePorts.
how: The preload forwards ipcRenderer messages that carry ports to the page with window.postMessage(...,"*",e.ports) for "transcript:port" and a second port channel; claude-page host-tools use "claude-page:host-tools-hello/port" handshake messages; the main process creates MessageChannelMain pairs for utility-process MCP hosts, framebuffer previews and PTY streams (sites at L36893, L50172, L61633, L107867). Utility processes receive their port through process.parentPort.once("message").
verevonRelevance: Model Plane streaming (tokens, tool output, screen frames) should use a dedicated binary/stream channel (WebSocket or WebTransport) distinct from control RPC; the same two-lane split is visible here.

name: Utility-process worker fleet with explicit message protocols
what: CPU- or I/O-heavy work runs in separate utility processes or workers so the main thread stays responsive: PTY host, login-shell PATH resolver, transcript search, file index, git/heavy work, MSAL broker, stall sampler, and the MCP hosts.
how: Files under .vite/build: pty-host/ptyHostWorker.js (spawn, write, resize, kill, read-scrollback, dispose-scrollback, shutdown), shell-path-worker, transcript-search-worker (search, readTranscript, extractInferenceLogIds), file-index-worker (gitignore-aware index for @-mentions), heavy-work-worker (git plumbing, key operations), msal-broker-worker (acquireTokenSilent/Interactive, getAllAccounts, signOut), stall-sampler-worker, mcp-runtime/nodeHost.js and directMcpHost.js. utilityProcess.fork is called at core L36535 and L61627 with PATH normalised first. Each worker installs uncaughtException handlers that exit rather than hang.
evidence: REA ev_ad009afc4495e7b69f7e22b6972460adddac00cd2353e0dffe449d0da4bea7c8 (analyze_javascript_application summary of main/preload/worker subset: context_bridge_apis 52, IPC operations 1504 of which 9 literal and 1495 dynamic, renderer_transmissions 1278, renderer_listeners 226, semantic coverage partial)
verevonRelevance: A Rust port gets this almost for free with tokio tasks or child processes; the useful design rule is that every worker speaks a closed set of typed messages and dies on unhandled errors.

name: Main-thread stall profiler using a shared heartbeat and the V8 inspector
what: When the main thread freezes, the app captures a CPU profile of the stall without paying profiler cost during normal operation.
how: The main thread increments a BigInt64Array heartbeat; a worker polls it with Atomics.load, and if the beat stops for stallThresholdMs it starts an inspector Profiler session (connectToMainThread), stops after maxCaptureMs or when the beat resumes, summarises top frames by self time and posts a stall_capture message. A token bucket (maxBurstCaptures, minCaptureIntervalMs) bounds capture rate.
verevonRelevance: Cheap field diagnostics for the Verevon desktop shell: heartbeat plus on-demand sampling in a separate thread is portable to Rust (shared atomic plus a sampling thread).

name: Startup performance: precomputed V8 code cache and lazy-loaded SDK and bridge chunks
what: The app starts faster by loading main-bundle bytecode from a precompiled cache and by deferring the heavy Agent SDK and Remote Control bridge code until first use.
how: index.pre.js overrides Module.prototype._compile to wrap each build file in vm.Script with cachedData read from compile-cache/<file>.<arch>.jsc (files exist for index.js, index.chunk-Xi8kaA5n.js and the core chunk); status is recorded as hit/miss/partial on globalThis.__claudeMainCompileCache and the cache is generated at build time under CLAUDE_GENERATE_COMPILE_CACHE. The SDK (index.chunk-D6Q00DJz.js) and bridge (index.chunk-DcP6Ha83.js) are loaded through dynamic requires via loadAgentSdk/loadAgentSdkBridge with load-time logging.
verevonRelevance: Irrelevant for a native Rust shell, but the principle (measure cold-start, split rarely used heavy modules) applies to the SolidJS bundle and to lazy-loading Model Plane client modules.
notes: About 330 hashed index.chunk files; most are vendor/feature splits with no semantic names.

name: Privileged custom URL schemes and per-purpose session partitions
what: Local content (artifacts, files, media, simulator frames) is served from app-owned schemes so it can be sandboxed separately from the web UI.
how: registerSchemesAsPrivileged declares cowork-artifact (standard, secure, fetch), cowork-file (stream), claude-media (stream, bypassCSP) and claude-simulator (stream, bypassCSP, cors). Each scheme is bound to its own session partition (persist:cowork-artifact-<id>, persist:cowork-file-preview; file-preview and artifact sessions deny every permission request and permission check; a claude-media handler serves session images/video). A fifth scheme, app://localhost, serves the bundled UI in third-party mode.
verevonRelevance: Model-generated HTML/Markdown artifacts in Verevon should render from an isolated origin/partition with permissions denied by default, as done here.

name: Single-instance lock, multi-brand deep-link schemes and cold-start deep-link delivery
what: Opening a claude:// link focuses the running app and routes to the right surface even when the web UI has not finished loading; separate brands/dev builds use their own schemes.
how: requestSingleInstanceLock gates app ready; a second-instance handler dedupes repeated argv, resolves the link and delivers it via the claudeURLHandler once the main view is ready (cold-start flag and an argvCapped flag for the Windows command-line limit). Accepted schemes: claude:, claude-dev:, claude-nest:, claude-nest-dev:, claude-nest-prod:. A setting can disable deep-link handling.
verevonRelevance: Needed for any Verevon desktop wrapper (open a run or a Space from a link); the cold-start queue is the non-obvious part.

name: Parallel build flavours (prod, dev, Store, Nest) with separate data roots and schemes
what: Several variants of the app can be installed side by side without sharing data, including an internal prototype flavour called Nest.
how: Build info JSON (commitHash, buildType prod/dev, isNestBuild, isStoreBuild, appVersion) is baked into the bundle and validated with zod; user-data candidates are enumerated for both "Claude" and "Claude Nest" roots (Roaming and Local); dev tooling appends -msstore / -nest suffixes; Nest-only prototypes are initialised at startup and torn down by cleanupNestOnlyPrototypes.
verevonRelevance: Verevon likely needs prod/staging/dev flavours with isolated data roots and deep-link schemes from day one.
notes: Nest purpose is inferred (an internal or alternate-brand build); only the flavour plumbing was read.

name: Windows MSIX identity, Squirrel fallback and MSIX file-system devirtualisation
what: On Windows the app ships as an MSIX package (with a Squirrel path for non-Store installs) and works around MSIX's per-package file redirection so user data and VM mounts resolve to real paths.
how: Startup branches on Qr() (isMsix): appends "MSIX" to the user agent, sets the AppUserModelId from the package family, handles --squirrel-* events, and calls initMsixDevirtualization(userData); helper functions devirtualizeMsixPath, guestCompatibleRootPath and fromGuestCompatibleRootPath convert redirected paths for VM mounts; native getCurrentPackageFamilyName/isCurrentPackageBeingServiced are used by the VM-service client and the updater.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships an MSIX build, path virtualisation will break agent file mounts unless handled; plan for it.

name: First-party update service with channels, idle-aware checks, delta payloads and version caps
what: Updates come from Anthropic's own update API rather than a public feed, can be set to a stable or latest channel, avoid interrupting busy users, and can be capped or disabled by IT.
how: The feed URL is https://<api host>/api/desktop/<platform>/<arch-or-universal>/<msix|squirrel>/update?...&channelUuid=<id> (releases.claude.com when updateViaUpdatesHost is set); MSIX uses serverType json. A preference called ancientJournal (stable|latest) selects the channel and is gated by a feature flag. Checks are throttled: the host tracks busy time and unfocused time and only checks when quiet (or after a long busy stretch). dangerousMaxVersion caps updates; disableAutoUpdates and a 72-hour enforcement window are in the managed registry; staged payload kind (zip, delta, delta_fell_back) is persisted for diagnostics; the AutoUpdater service exposes restartToUpdateWhenIdle and running-session counts so the restart waits for local sessions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's agent runs are long-lived; copy the idea of deferring restart until running sessions are idle and exposing the count to the UI.
notes: The CLI auto-updater is disabled for MSIX installs (see the Claude Code binary management record).

name: Managed Claude Code binary distribution with a signed release manifest and staged rollout
what: The desktop app downloads, verifies and updates its own copy of the Claude Code engine, independent of any terminal install, and refuses updates that fail signature, compatibility or flag checks.
how: The bundle embeds a release catalog (version 2.1.295, baseUrl downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases, sdkWrapperVersion 0.3.295, per-platform checksum/size for claude.zst or claude.exe.zst, sdkCompat.testedWrapperVersions, harnessSchema 1). The poller (wakes hourly with +-10 percent jitter and performs a real check every N ticks, default 4 and remotely reducible, starting with an immediate check; flag-gated; disabled for MSIX installs and by enterprise policy; skipped when feature flags are stale for over two hours) fetches /stable, then <version>/manifest.zst.json plus a .raw-sig.json sidecar, verifies an RSA-SHA512 signature over "claude-code-manifest-v1\0"+bytes with an embedded public key (checks schema, algorithm, canonical base64, key id), validates version floor, manifest/wrapper compatibility and harnessSchema, optionally spreads rollout over N hours using sha256(installId, version) mod window, then installs and swaps the host target. A local binary override and a separate VM copy path exist.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon embeds a coding/agent engine as a child process, this is the model to follow: pinned compatibility matrix between host wrapper and engine, signed manifests with domain separation, stale-flag gating and deterministic per-install rollout spreading.
notes: manifestSignatureEnforcement is "flag" (not hard-enforced) in this build. DOC corroboration: the desktop app runs its own copy of Claude Code that can differ from the terminal CLI (code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop, fetched 2026-10-13).

name: Persistent state map: where the desktop stores configuration, sessions, caches and secrets
what: State is spread over a conventional userData layout with human-readable JSON for configuration and separate directories for sessions, extensions, VM bundles, worktrees and caches.
how: From path joins in the bundle: config.json and claude_desktop_config.json (settings and MCP servers), developer_settings.json, window-state.json, scheduled-tasks.json, git-worktrees.json, extensions-installations.json, extensions-blocklist.json, directories Claude Extensions, Claude Extensions Settings, Extensions Update Cache, local-agent-mode-sessions, claude-code-sessions, claude-code, claude-code-vm, ccd-session-secrets, cowork-managed, cowork-user-files, cowork-file-preview, git-shadow, uv-runtime, plugin-cache, skills-plugin, marketplace-plugin-assets, pending-uploads, remote-bash-outputs, simulator-builds, sim-recordings, framebuffer-ledgers, ChromeNativeHost, sentry, logs, traces, crashDumps, Partitions. electron-store/conf serialise JSON; safeStorage encrypts secrets; the account storage dir can override the sessions root.

notes: Names come from path constants only; no user data directory was read.

name: Preference schema where every key declares whether the Claude agent may read or modify it
what: Settings are classified by who may touch them. Security-relevant preferences are marked as excluded from Claude's own settings tool, and a set of keys can only be changed by main-process code, never by the web page.
how: The zod preferences schema attaches meta(qh(reason)) = {claudeAccess:{kind:"excluded",reason}} to keys (reason "security" or "other"); setPreferenceFromRenderer validates each inbound key with its own sub-schema, rejects keys in MAIN_ONLY_PREFERENCE_KEYS (folder grants, trusted folders, secure VM flag, preview allowlists, etc.), enforces monotonic-reduction rules for some map keys and fires side effects (the computer-use toggle reloads the remote tool host and logs cu_setting_changed).
verevonRelevance: Directly applicable: Verevon should tag every setting with agent-writable yes/no plus reason so that a model-facing "settings" tool can never alter grants, egress rules or credentials.
notes: The agent-facing settings tool visible in this very harness (get_settings/set_setting) is consistent with this design (INF).

name: Declarative managed-settings registry with legacy-key migration, fail-closed values and egress declarations
what: Every enterprise-configurable key is described once with its registry name, scopes, default, title, grouping, show/warn predicates, what to do when the key is unreadable, and which network hosts the feature needs.
how: Entries are created with H(zodSchema,{flatKey,support:{enabled:{scopes:["1p","3p"],availableInVersion},executionTarget},title,default,legacyFlatKey:{name,effect},failClosedValue,egressRequirements,category,group,order,description,predicates:{show,warn}}). Example: isDesktopExtensionEnabled defaults false with egress requirements for the Python runtime; isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired fails closed to true; disableAutoUpdates warns that fixes will not install automatically. The same registry drives the admin UI (Custom3pSetup) and validation. 70 keys, mostly scope 3p.
verevonRelevance: A schema-first admin surface where each setting carries its own fail-closed value and required egress hosts is exactly what Verevon's Control Plane policy engine needs for enterprise tenants.

name: Managed-config tiers: OS policy (HKLM/HKCU, MDM profile, root-owned file) merged with local settings
what: IT can control the app through the registry, an MDM profile or a root-owned file, and the app says which source it used and disables local settings when the managed tier is unusable.
how: Windows policy keys are read under SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude (HKCU and HKLM) via the native addon's readRegistryValues/enumRegistryValues; macOS uses the MDM preference domain and Linux /etc/claude-desktop/managed-settings.json (labels: MDM profile, GPO registry policy, etc_file). Unreadable or malformed managed configuration disables local settings (fail closed) and is reported. A separate path hierarchy configures the embedded Claude Code (C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode or C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode, /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode, /etc/claude-code; managed-settings.json plus managed-settings.d and remote-settings.json).

verevonRelevance: Verevon's Control Plane will need an equivalent for on-prem/desktop clients; the explicit "source" label and fail-closed behaviour are worth copying.

name: Feature flags through GrowthBook with a layered source chain and numeric flag IDs
what: Features roll out remotely. Flags are resolved from a live fetch, a disk cache or a hard-coded fallback, are logged as exposures, and can be forced to a static map for third-party deployments.
how: GrowthBook client initialisation picks a source (static map for 3p, remote refresh, disk cache, map-fallback), refreshes on a schedule and on account change, and clears per-account exposure sets; flags are addressed by obfuscated numeric hashes (Hv("762798616"), Vv(id,default)); exposure events (desktop_feature_exposure, GrowthbookExperimentEvent) are batched with telemetry; several security gates require fresh flags (staleness windows of two hours for CLI auto-update, about 90 minutes for computer-use rollout). KV() produces the per-window feature table of 122 keys with statuses.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane needs the same: tenant/user flags with fallback chain and freshness requirements on risky capabilities (computer use, remote control).
notes: Flag names are hashed, so meaning is inferred from call sites; codenames in the scout inventory are low confidence.

name: Telemetry pipeline with batching, jitter, org-aware scrubbing and a hard off switch
what: Usage events are queued locally and flushed in batches, never in CI, never when nonessential telemetry is disabled, and with extra scrubbing for HIPAA organisations.
how: Events accumulate in an in-memory queue and flush on a timer (60 s to 10 min, randomised 0.5x-1.5x) and on quit to POST {api}/api/event_logging/v2/batch with header x-service-name: claude_desktop and bearer/cookie credentials depending on sign-in state; 401/403 triggers credential refresh; Sentry is separate. disableNonessential blocks upload, CI runs withhold events, strings are sanitised with toWellFormed, and HIPAA orgs call event.rescrub(originOrgId) before send. A periodic app-metrics digest (RSS, heap, renderer and GPU memory) is attached.
verevonRelevance: Reuse the pattern (queue, jittered flush, per-org rescrub hook, kill switch) for Verevon product telemetry; align rescrubbing with Zero-Data-Retention propagation.

name: Allow-list based telemetry and log scrubbing library
what: Names of tools, plugins, MCP servers, skills and marketplaces are reported only when they are known first-party names; everything user-defined becomes a sentinel or a salted hash, and paths, emails, IPs and secrets are scrubbed from free text and support bundles.
how: A shared module exports redactToolName, redactMcpServerName/Url, redactPluginId (salted hash PLUGIN_ID_HASH_SALT), redactDxtExtensionId, redactSkillName, redactBedrockArnAccountId, redactEmail, redactIpAddress, redactEmbeddedUrlsToHost, scrubFilesystemPaths, scrubFreeText, scrubLogLine, scrubBufferForBundle, deepScrubStrings, stripUrlUserinfo and constants CUSTOM_SERVER_SENTINEL and SAFE_QUERY_PARAMS (query-param allow-list, with a variant without click IDs).
verevonRelevance: Verevon observability should adopt allow-list naming (known names only, sentinel otherwise) so tenant-defined tool and connector names never leak into shared telemetry.

name: Third-party deployment mode: bundled UI served from app://localhost over a stub backend
what: For Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or gateway deployments the app does not load claude.ai; it serves a bundled copy of the web UI from the install folder and answers the API calls that UI would make from a local shim.

The handler injects a per-response Content-Security-Policy built from managed config (Anthropic host, artifact iframe host, dictation endpoint, update host) and window.__DESKTOP_3P_PUBLIC_CONFIG__. Stubs answer /api/bootstrap (and /app_start, /system_prompts, /current_user_access), plugin and marketplace lists, dust/command_display_names, dust/generate_session_title and generate_title_and_branch (title generation runs through the configured provider), i18n files; some paths are forwarded to the Anthropic host with 503 conversion on failure; everything else returns a JSON "custom_3p_not_available" 503.

name: Deployment-profile model: one config object selects provider, credential kind and managed MCP servers
what: A single declarative profile chooses how the app reaches models (Anthropic, gateway, Vertex, Bedrock, Mantle, Foundry), how it authenticates, which models are offered, which MCP servers are force-installed and how long sessions live.

Validation errors are typed (tVe) and credentials are loaded once and cached.

name: Secrets never ride in the agent environment: per-session secret files and credential scrubbing
what: Provider credentials for third-party mode are written to a short-lived per-session directory and handed to the engine by file, while stray credential variables are stripped from the engine's environment.

verevonRelevance: Verevon sandboxes should receive credentials via a mounted short-lived file or an RPC callback, never as plain environment variables visible to tools.
notes: No secret values were read; only code paths and variable names.

name: Identity-verified local pipes: SYSTEM-owned VM service pipe and same-user Chrome pipe
what: Before the app talks to the VM service or the Chrome extension over a Windows named pipe it checks who owns the server end, so another process cannot impersonate either.

name: Safe file open through native containment instead of path-based fs calls
what: File access that must stay inside a granted folder uses an openat-style call from the native addon, and the app refuses to degrade to a normal path open if the addon fails to load.

Sessions are signed with device-bound keys (DeviceRegistry: signCreateSessionBind, signSessionBind, signConversationBind, getPublicKey, rotateKey).

name: Generic utility-process supervisor with proof-of-health, cooldown backoff and request correlation
what: Background workers are started lazily, restarted with exponential cooldown if they crash, and a request that hangs kills the worker instead of blocking the app.
how: A reusable worker client forks a utilityProcess with serviceName and piped stdio, creates a MessageChannelMain, sends an init message carrying one port, correlates replies by numeric requestId in a pending map, treats an initial reply as proof the worker is healthy (cooldown.proven), applies cooldown backoff on early exits or kills with a request in flight (reject all pending as worker_killed/worker_unavailable), logs worker stdout/stderr through the main logger and re-sends pending port transfers after refork. One worker bundle (heavy-work-worker) is instantiated as many named pools, each with an OS-visible serviceName, a QoS policy and its own RPC timeout: heavy-work (2 min), worktree-copy (30 min), scratch-carry, heavy-work-archive (15 min), storage-scan (5 min), spaces-inventory (2 min), config-read (30 s), key-convert (1 min), terminal-screen (5 s), git (2 min), transcript-read, diagnostics-read (30 s), cowork-archive (1 h), dispatch-census, dispatch-history-read, tombstone-remove (1 h) and simulator-accessibility (30 s). QoS classes: read-only (no kill on timeout, concurrent), serialised-mutating (requests serialised by a mutex, worker killed on timeout) and kill-on-timeout concurrent.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane's local tool workers (file index, search, sandbox helpers) should sit behind one supervisor type with backoff and health proof instead of ad-hoc restarts.

name: System CA store and proxy awareness for fetch, child processes and MCP servers
what: Corporate TLS-inspection certificates and proxies work for the app, the engine and extensions without manual setup.
how: The app reads the OS certificate store through Node getCACertificates("system") (prewarmed when idle, with a bounded retry loop), builds NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS/NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1 for forked Node-based extensions, resolves HTTP(S) proxies from the system (SOCKS entries are skipped with a warning because downstream HTTP agents cannot use them), and exposes a "Network reachability" diagnostic and egress probe; the Windows VM service additionally injects host trusted roots into the guest.
verevonRelevance: Enterprise desktop agents fail first on TLS interception and proxies; plan system-CA and PAC support in the Rust HTTP stack (rustls-platform-verifier / reqwest) from the start.

name: Login-shell environment capture so GUI-launched processes see the user's real PATH
what: Apps started from the Dock/Start menu do not inherit the shell profile; the app runs the user's login shell once to learn PATH and a fixed set of Claude variables.
how: A shell-path worker runs $SHELL -l -i -c with markers and env -0 (5 s timeout, minimal env, SSH_AUTH_SOCK kept), parses the null-separated environment, drops PWD/OLDPWD/SHLVL/_ and a few helper variables, and the main process primes process.env from it (primeProcessEnvFromLoginShell) at startup; on Windows a native readFreshUserPath reads the user PATH from the registry.

name: Renderer-driven native window manager with allow-listed properties and caps
what: The web UI can ask the shell to create and control additional native windows, but only with a vetted set of properties and within hard limits.

verevonRelevance: A pattern for Verevon desktop: let the web UI request windows declaratively but filter properties through an allow-list and cap counts.

name: Windows service lifecycle from an unprivileged client: SCM probing, classified outcomes and exponential start backoff
what: The app starts the VM service through the Service Control Manager when it is stopped, interprets Win32 error codes, avoids starting during package servicing and backs off so a broken service does not cause start storms.
how: probe: queryWindowsServiceState maps states (not_installed, stopped, start_pending, stop_pending, running, paused, other); the client waits out stop_pending, skips start if the MSIX package is being serviced, calls startWindowsService with a deadline, and classifies the outcome (running, denied for error 5, failed with codes 1058/1060/1072, exited, timeout, skipped_servicing); a backoff object (5 s to 5 min) and a "not asking the SCM again for N s" window prevent repeated attempts; the verdicts drive whether to redial the pipe, retry or fail with "restart your computer".
verevonRelevance: The same pattern fits any Verevon Windows helper service: classify SCM outcomes, respect servicing, backoff, and keep the user message actionable.

name: One managed-config schema served to several clients (desktop, Microsoft 365 add-in, Claude Code CLI)
what: The same enterprise configuration document is consumed by the desktop app, the Claude add-in for Microsoft 365 and the Claude Code CLI, each with its own served schema version.
how: A consumer registry lists desktop (served schema version 2, reads bootstrap), m365 (version 2, typePrefix M365) and code (the CLI signed in by itself, served false in this build); registry entries declare readers per key; remote policy metadata (type remote-only, hybrid scope excluded/only/derived, hotApplied) controls which keys can be delivered remotely and applied without restart; provider labels map gateway/anthropic/bedrock/mantle/vertex/foundry to display names and credential kinds are ordered by preference lists.
verevonRelevance: Treat Verevon's web, desktop and add-in clients as consumers of one tenant policy schema with per-client served versions, rather than per-client settings.

name: Office add-in sideloading and bridge: WEF trusted catalog, per-file manifests and conversation handoff
what: The desktop can open a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file, sideload Claude's Office add-in into it, wait for the add-in to connect over the bridge and then drive it with office_addin tools or hand a conversation over to it.

name: Teleport a local session to the cloud: readiness check, plan, push-based transfer with progress and failure events
what: A local Code session can be moved to a cloud environment after the app checks readiness and shows a plan of what will be transferred.
how: LocalSessions exposes getTeleportReadiness(sessionId), getTeleportPlan(sessionId,{includeUntracked}), teleportToCloud(sessionId, environmentId,{skipPush, transport "push"...}) and resolveCloudBranch(folder) (requires a trusted cwd and resolves repo ids through the GitHub PR layer); progress is pushed to the renderer as teleport_progress and teleport_upload_failed events (command and error excerpt); notes in the git layer explain that after a push the branch comparison is unavailable until a host-side fetch retrieves the objects.

name: Account- and org-scoped storage tree with Windows short-path compaction and dual-path compatibility
what: Local state is partitioned per account and organisation, and on Windows long UUID folder names can be shortened to avoid path-length failures without losing data that already exists under the long names.
how: The sessions root userData/local-agent-mode-sessions/<accountId>/<orgId> holds scheduled-tasks.json, spaces.json, remote-session-spaces.json, cowork-gb-cache.json (flag cache), cowork-clientdata-cache.json, cowork-policy-limits-cache.json, cowork_settings.json, cowork_account_settings.json, a usage-ledger folder and sibling trees keyed the same way (library-submissions, cowork-session-seed/artifact-roster.json, scheduled-task-grants/artifact-publish-grants.json, usage-metrics/pending.json offline queue, plugin-cache, plugin-command, skills-plugin). When short-path mode is enabled, UUID components are cut to their first 8 hex digits (local_<uuid> becomes the 8-digit form); a resolver decides per account/org whether the short or full directory is authoritative by probing which exists (never creating a conflict, throwing "session storage folder name is occupied" if both clash) and caches the decision, so migration is incremental and reversible.
verevonRelevance: Verevon desktop caches keyed by tenant/user should plan for Windows MAX_PATH from the start (short stable ids plus dual-path resolution), and keep per-tenant caches (flags, policy limits, usage ledger) isolated by directory.
notes: Directory names come from path-builder code only; nothing was listed from a user data directory.

name: Artifact frame shell with a pinned runtime and a separate renderer origin for untrusted content
what: Artifacts rendered inside the web UI load through a minimal "frame shell" page whose runtime is pinned by a manifest and which can live on its own origin, so model-authored content never shares an origin with the app.
how: The bundled ion-dist ships frame-shell.html (24.6 KB, title "Artifact", meta frame-runtime-pin = manifest id, referrer no-referrer, noindex), frame-connect.html and frame-manage.html (about 1.6 KB each) and an _frame-rt/_runtime folder; in third-party mode the host reads workspace.userContentRendererUrl from managed config, injects its origin into window.__DESKTOP_3P_PUBLIC_CONFIG__ and adds the artifact iframe host to the per-response CSP; custom-3p-gated-imports.json (buildId "spa-dev") gates dynamic imports for that build.
verevonRelevance: Render Verevon artifacts from a separate registrable origin through a pinned, versioned frame runtime; it removes whole classes of cross-origin attacks on the chat page.
notes: The runtime and frame protocol inside the minified ion-dist assets were not analysed; only the shell metadata and host wiring were read.
